translations.literal: Sun Shao, Zhang Puhui, Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Lu Yu, Zhang Yao, Liu Daobin, Dong Shao, Feng Yuanxing
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao, Zhang Puhui, Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Lu Yu, Zhang Yao, Liu Daobin, Dong Shao, and Feng Yuanxing

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Thirty-four
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 34

sentences.zh: 孫紹張普惠成淹范紹劉桃符鹿悆張耀劉道斌董紹馮元興

translations.literal: Sun Shao, Zhang Puhui, Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Lu Yu, Zhang Yao, Liu Daobin, Dong Shao, Feng Yuanxing
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao, Zhang Puhui, Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Lu Yu, Zhang Yao, Liu Daobin, Dong Shao, and Feng Yuanxing

sentences.zh: 孫紹，字世慶，昌黎人也。

translations.literal: Sun Shao, style name Shiqing, was a man of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao, courtesy name Shiqing, was from Changli.

sentences.zh: 少好學，通涉經史。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From an early age he loved study and gained a thorough command of the classics and historical works.

sentences.zh: 初為校書郎，稍遷給事中，後為門下錄事。

translations.literal: He first served as collator, was gradually promoted to attendant within the gates, and later became recorder of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a collator, was gradually promoted to attendant within the gates, and later became a recorder in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 好言得失，與常景共修律令。

translations.literal: He liked to speak of what was right and wrong in policy, and together with Chang Jing he revised the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of speaking frankly about policy successes and failures, and together with Chang Jing he worked on revising the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，紹表曰：

translations.literal: In the Yanxi era, Shao submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxi period, Shao submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞建國有計，雖危必安；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when founding a state there is a plan, and though in peril it must be made secure;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a state is founded with a clear plan, it can be secured even in peril;

sentences.zh: 施化能和，雖寡必盛；

translations.literal: when transforming influence can achieve harmony, though few it must flourish;
translations.idiomatic: when governance achieves harmony, a small realm will still flourish;

sentences.zh: 政乖人理，雖合必離；

translations.literal: when government departs from human reason, though united it must split apart;
translations.idiomatic: when policy runs counter to human nature, even a united realm will fall apart;

sentences.zh: 作用失機，雖成必敗。

translations.literal: when action misses its moment, though successful it must fail.
translations.idiomatic: and when action misses its moment, even apparent success ends in defeat.

sentences.zh: 此乃古今同然，百王之定法也。

translations.literal: This is the same in ancient and modern times—the fixed law of a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: This has been true in every age; it is the unchanging principle by which all kings have ruled.

sentences.zh: 今二虢京門，了無嚴防；

translations.literal: Now at the two Guo capital gates there is utterly no strict defense;
translations.idiomatic: Today the two capital gates at Guo have scarcely any serious defense;

sentences.zh: 南北二中，復闕固守；

translations.literal: at the northern and southern secondary centers, firm holding is again lacking;
translations.idiomatic: the northern and southern secondary centers likewise lack solid garrisons;

sentences.zh: 長安、鄴城，股肱之寄；

translations.literal: Chang'an and Yecheng are the trust of the arms and legs;
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an and Yecheng are entrusted as the state's right and left arms;

sentences.zh: 穰城、上黨，腹背所馮。

translations.literal: Rangcheng and Shangdang are what the belly and back lean upon.
translations.idiomatic: Rangcheng and Shangdang support the realm from front and rear.

sentences.zh: 四軍、五校之軌，領、護分事之式，徵兵儲粟之要，舟車水陸之資，山河要害之權，緩急去來之用，持平赴救之方，節用應時之法，特宜修置，以固堂堂之基。

translations.literal: The tracks of the four armies and five commandants, the forms by which commanders and protectors divide duties, the essentials of levying troops and storing grain, the resources of boats, carts, water, and land routes, the authority of mountain and river strongpoints, the uses of coming and going in urgency and calm, the methods of balanced relief and rescue, and the laws of frugal expenditure suited to the times—all especially ought to be established and repaired to solidify the august foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The organization of the four armies and five commandants, the division of duties among commanders and protectors, the levying of troops and storage of grain, transport by land and water, control of strategic passes, provisions for emergencies, balanced relief measures, and timely economies—all of these urgently need to be put in order to secure the foundations of our great state.

sentences.zh: 持盈之體，何得而忽？

translations.literal: The body that holds fullness—how can it be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: How can we neglect the task of preserving a realm already at its height?

sentences.zh: 且法開清濁，而清濁不平；

translations.literal: Moreover the law distinguishes pure and base, yet pure and base are not level;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the law distinguishes noble and common ranks, noble and common are not treated equally;

sentences.zh: 申滯理望，而卑寒亦免。

translations.literal: stagnation is explained and expectations regulated, yet the lowly and cold are also exempted.
translations.idiomatic: and though regulations are meant to clear blockages and set fair expectations, the humble and poor are also exempted.

sentences.zh: 士庶同悲，兵徒懷怨。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners alike grieve; soldiers and conscripts harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners alike lament, while soldiers and conscripts nurse grievances.

sentences.zh: 中正賣望於下里，主案舞筆於上臺，真偽混淆，知而不糾，得者不欣，失者倍怨。

translations.literal: Rectifiers sell reputation in the villages; chief clerks flourish their brushes at the high desk; true and false are confused, known yet not corrected; those who gain are not glad, and those who lose are doubly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Rectifiers sell favors in the countryside, chief clerks manipulate records at court, truth and falsehood are confused, wrongdoing is known yet left uncorrected, those who gain show no joy, and those who lose are twice as bitter.

sentences.zh: 使門齊身等而涇、渭奄殊，類應同役而苦樂縣異，士人居職，不以為榮；

translations.literal: It makes families of equal standing suddenly as different as the Jing and Wei rivers, and categories that ought to share the same service separated by vast differences in hardship and ease; gentlemen in office do not regard it as honor;
translations.idiomatic: Families of equal standing are suddenly divided as sharply as the Jing and Wei rivers, men of the same category who should share the same service suffer vastly unequal hardship, and gentlemen in office no longer regard their posts as an honor;

sentences.zh: 兵士役苦，必不忘亂。

translations.literal: soldiers laboring bitterly in service will surely not forget rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: while soldiers crushed by harsh service will never forget the urge to revolt.

sentences.zh: 故有競棄本生，飄藏他土。

translations.literal: Therefore some compete to abandon their native livelihood and drift to hide in other lands.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason many abandon their native homes and flee to other regions.

sentences.zh: 或詭名托養，散沒人間；

translations.literal: Some use false names and entrust themselves for support, scattering and vanishing among the people;
translations.idiomatic: Some take false names and live under others' protection, scattering invisibly among the populace;

sentences.zh: 或亡命山藪，漁獵為命；

translations.literal: some flee their lives into mountains and marshes and make fishing and hunting their livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: some flee into the mountains and marshes and live by fishing and hunting;

sentences.zh: 或投杖強豪，寄命衣食。

translations.literal: some cast aside their staffs and throw themselves on powerful families, entrusting their lives for food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: and some throw in their lot with powerful clans, depending on them for food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 又應遷之戶，逐樂諸州；

translations.literal: Again, households that ought to be relocated seek pleasure in various provinces;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile households that ought to be relocated drift wherever life is pleasant;

sentences.zh: 應留之徒，避寒歸暖。

translations.literal: those who ought to remain flee cold and return to warmth.
translations.idiomatic: and those who ought to stay behind leave the cold north for warmer lands.

sentences.zh: 職人子弟，隨榮浮游，南北東西，卜居莫定。

translations.literal: Sons of officeholders drift with glory and advantage, east, west, north, and south, divining where to dwell without settling.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of officials drift after advantage, roaming north, south, east, and west with no settled home.

sentences.zh: 關禁不修，任意取適，如此之徒，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Passes and barriers are not maintained; they go wherever they please—such people are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Border controls are neglected, and people go wherever they wish; their numbers are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 爪牙不復為用，百工爭棄其業。

translations.literal: Talons and fangs are no longer employed; the hundred crafts compete to abandon their trades.
translations.idiomatic: The state's instruments of force are no longer effective, and craftsmen everywhere abandon their trades.

sentences.zh: 混一之計，事實闕如；

translations.literal: Plans for unification are in fact lacking;
translations.idiomatic: Plans for unification are in truth absent;

sentences.zh: 考課之方，責辦無日；

translations.literal: methods of examination and assessment have no day set for fulfillment;
translations.idiomatic: methods of inspection and assessment have no fixed deadline;

sentences.zh: 流浪之徒，決須精校。

translations.literal: wandering persons must decisively be carefully checked.
translations.idiomatic: and the wandering population must be rigorously registered.

sentences.zh: 今強敵窺時，邊黎伺隙，內人不平，久戍懷怨。

translations.literal: Now strong enemies watch for the moment, frontier peoples watch for openings, those within are not at peace, and long garrison troops harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Strong enemies now watch for their moment, frontier peoples watch for openings, the realm within is unsettled, and troops on long frontier service nurse bitter grievances.

sentences.zh: 戰國之勢，竊謂危矣。

translations.literal: The situation of the Warring States—I venture to say it is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The situation resembles that of the Warring States era, and I venture to say it is perilous.

sentences.zh: 必造禍源者，北邊鎮戍之人也。

translations.literal: Those who will surely create the source of calamity are the men of the northern frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The source of calamity will surely be the men of the northern frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 若夫一統之年，持平用之者，大道之計也；

translations.literal: As for years of unification, employing balance and fairness—that is the plan of the great Way;
translations.idiomatic: In years of unification, to govern with balance and fairness is the plan of the great Way;

sentences.zh: 亂離之期，縱橫作之者，行權之勢也。

translations.literal: in periods of disorder and separation, those who act with maneuver and alliance—that is the force of exercising expedient power.
translations.idiomatic: but in times of disorder and division, to act through alliances and maneuver is the force of expedient rule.

sentences.zh: 故道不可久，須文質以換情；

translations.literal: Therefore the Way cannot long endure unchanged; ornament and substance must be exchanged to shift sentiment;
translations.idiomatic: The Way cannot long remain unchanged; ornament and substance must alternate to meet the temper of the age;

sentences.zh: 權不可恆，隨汙隆以牧物。

translations.literal: expedient power cannot be constant; one must shepherd things according to whether the age is base or exalted.
translations.idiomatic: and expedient power cannot be fixed; one must govern according to whether the times are declining or rising.

sentences.zh: 文質應世，道形自安；

translations.literal: When ornament and substance respond to the age, the form of the Way is naturally secure;
translations.idiomatic: When ornament and substance suit the age, the Way finds its secure form;

sentences.zh: 汙隆獲衷，權勢亦濟。

translations.literal: when base and exalted obtain the mean, expedient power is also fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: when decline and ascent reach their proper balance, expedient power also succeeds.

sentences.zh: 然則王者計法之趣，化物之規，圓方務得其境，人物不失其地。

translations.literal: Thus the aim of the king's methods of planning and the rule for transforming things is that round and square each attain their proper realm and that people and things do not lose their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the king's methods aim to transform all things so that each form finds its proper place and neither people nor institutions lose their proper footing.

sentences.zh: 又先帝時，律、令並議，律尋施行，令獨不出，十餘年矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the former emperor's time both statutes and ordinances were deliberated; the statutes were soon put into effect, but the ordinances alone were not issued, and this has been more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the late emperor both statutes and ordinances were drafted; the statutes were soon promulgated, but the ordinances alone were never issued, and more than ten years have passed.

sentences.zh: 臣以令之為體，即帝王之身，分處百揆之儀，安置九服之節，乃是有為之樞機，世法之大本也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the substance of ordinances is the body of the emperor himself—the rites by which the hundred offices are apportioned, the regulations by which the nine domains are ordered; they are the pivot of purposeful action and the great foundation of the law of the age.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that ordinances are the very body of imperial rule—the rites apportioning the hundred offices, the regulations ordering the nine domains; they are the pivot of governance and the great foundation of the law of the age.

sentences.zh: 然修令之人，亦皆博古，依古撰置，大體可觀，比之前令，精粗有在。

translations.literal: Yet those who revised the ordinances were all broadly learned in antiquity; following antiquity they composed and arranged them, and in the main they are worth viewing; compared with earlier ordinances, there is substance in both refinement and roughness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who drafted the ordinances were all deeply learned in antiquity; following ancient models they composed a text that is on the whole impressive, and compared with earlier ordinances it shows real improvement in both refinement and scope.

sentences.zh: 但主議之家，大用古制。

translations.literal: But the families leading the deliberation relied heavily on ancient institutions.
translations.idiomatic: But the leading deliberators relied too heavily on ancient institutions.

sentences.zh: 若令依古，高祖之法，復須升降，誰敢措意有是非哉？

translations.literal: If the ordinances follow antiquity, the laws of Emperor Gaozu would again need to be raised and lowered—who would dare set his mind to right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: If the ordinances follow antiquity to the letter, even the laws of Emperor Gaozu would need revision—who would dare raise objections?

sentences.zh: 以是爭故，久廢不理。

translations.literal: Because of such contention they have long lain abandoned without being settled.
translations.idiomatic: Because of such disputes they have long lain abandoned without resolution.

sentences.zh: 然律、令相須，不可偏用，今律班令止，於事甚滯。

translations.literal: Yet statutes and ordinances depend on each other and cannot be used one-sidedly; now statutes are promulgated while ordinances are halted, which greatly impedes affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet statutes and ordinances depend on each other and cannot be used alone; now the statutes are promulgated while the ordinances are withheld, which greatly impedes governance.

sentences.zh: 若令不班，是無典法，臣下執事，何依而行？

translations.literal: If the ordinances are not promulgated, there is no canonical law—on what basis are subordinate officials to act?
translations.idiomatic: If the ordinances are not promulgated, there is no canonical law—on what basis are officials below to act?

sentences.zh: 臣等修律，非無勤止，署下之日，臣乃無名，是謂農夫盡力，他食其秋，功名之所，實懷於悒。

translations.literal: We who revised the statutes were not without diligence and effort, yet on the day of issuance your servant's name was absent—this is what is called the farmer exhausting his strength while another eats the harvest; as to where merit is recorded, I truly harbor dejection.
translations.idiomatic: We who revised the statutes labored diligently, yet on the day of promulgation my name was omitted—like the farmer who toils while another reaps the harvest; as to where credit is recorded, I am deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 正光初，兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang he concurrently served as vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengguang era he was appointed concurrent vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 紹性抗直，每上封事，常至懇切，不憚犯忤。

translations.literal: Shao's nature was upright and direct; whenever he submitted sealed memorials they were often utterly earnest, and he did not fear giving offense.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was upright and outspoken; his sealed memorials were always earnest, and he did not fear giving offense.

sentences.zh: 但天性疏脫，言乍高下，時人輕之，不見采覽。

translations.literal: But by nature he was loose and unguarded; his words suddenly rose and fell, and men of the time looked down on him—his views were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: But he was by nature careless in manner, his speech uneven in tone, and men of the time looked down on him; his views were not adopted.

sentences.zh: 紹兄世元善彈箏，早卒。

translations.literal: Shao's elder brother Shiyuan was skilled at playing the zheng and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's elder brother Shiyuan was skilled at the zheng harp and died young.

sentences.zh: 紹後聞箏聲，便涕泗鳴咽，舍之而去。

translations.literal: Later, when Shao heard the sound of the zheng, he would weep and sob and leave the place.
translations.idiomatic: Later, whenever Shao heard the zheng played, he would weep and leave the room.

sentences.zh: 後為太府少卿，曾因朝見，靈太后謂曰：「卿年稍老矣。」

translations.literal: Later he became vice director of the Imperial Storehouse; on one occasion when he attended court, Empress Dowager Ling said to him, "Your age is somewhat advanced."
translations.idiomatic: Later he became vice director of the Imperial Storehouse. Once at court audience, Empress Dowager Ling said to him, "You are getting on in years."

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「臣年雖老，臣卿乃少。」

translations.literal: Shao said, "Though your servant's years are old, your servant's wife is still young."
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied, "Though I am old, my wife is still young."

sentences.zh: 太后笑之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager laughed at this.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager laughed.

sentences.zh: 遷右將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 紹曾與百僚赴朝，東掖未開，守門候旦。

translations.literal: Shao once went to court with the hundred officials; the eastern side gate had not yet opened, and the gatekeepers waited for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Shao once went to court with the other officials. The eastern side gate had not yet opened, and the gatekeepers were waiting for dawn.

sentences.zh: 紹於眾中引吏部郎中辛雄于眾外，竊謂曰：「此中諸人，尋當死盡，唯吾與卿，猶享富貴。」

translations.literal: Shao drew Xin Xiong, director in the Ministry of Personnel, out from among the crowd and whispered, "All these people here will soon die to the last; only you and I will still enjoy wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Shao drew Xin Xiong, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, aside from the crowd and whispered, "Everyone here will soon be dead; only you and I will still enjoy wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 未幾，有河陰之難。

translations.literal: Before long came the calamity at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came the massacre at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 紹善推祿命，事驗甚多，知者異之。

translations.literal: Shao was skilled at calculating fate from emolument and destiny; events verified his predictions in many cases, and those who knew were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was skilled at calculating fate from birth and office records; events confirmed his predictions in many cases, and those who knew were astonished.

sentences.zh: 永安中，拜太府卿，以前參議《正光壬子曆》，賜爵新昌子。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was appointed director of the Imperial Storehouse; because he had earlier participated in deliberating the Zhengguang rensi calendar, he was granted the title Marquis of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he was appointed director of the Imperial Storehouse; for his earlier participation in drafting the Zhengguang rensi calendar, he was granted the title Marquis of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 後卒于右光祿大夫，贈尚書左僕射，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; he was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子伯元襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Boyuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boyuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 張普惠，字洪賑，常山九門人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Puhui, style name Hongzhen, was a man of Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Puhui, courtesy name Hongzhen, was from Jiumen in Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，容貌魁偉，精於《三禮》，兼善《春秋》、百家之說。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet in height, his appearance lofty and imposing; he was expert in the Three Rites and also skilled in the Spring and Autumn Annals and the teachings of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall, with a imposing bearing; he was expert in the Three Rites and also skilled in the Spring and Autumn Annals and the teachings of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 太和十九年，為主書，帶制局監，頗為孝文所知。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taihe he served as chief clerk, concurrently as supervisor of the drafting office, and was rather well known to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Taihe era he served as chief clerk with concurrent appointment as supervisor of the drafting office, and came to the attention of Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書都令史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄重其學業，為其聲價。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Ren-city valued his scholarship and enhanced his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Ren-city valued his scholarship and helped build his reputation.

sentences.zh: 澄為雍州刺史，啟普惠為府錄事參軍，尋行馮翊郡事。

translations.literal: When Cheng became governor of Yong province he recommended Puhui as recorder and staff adjutant of his headquarters, and soon had him administer the affairs of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng became governor of Yong province, he recommended Puhui as recorder-adjutant on his staff and soon had him administer Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 澄功衰在身，欲七月七日集文武北園馬射。

translations.literal: Cheng was in the declining period of mourning for his merit-relatives and wished on the seventh day of the seventh month to gather civil and military officials in the northern park for horse archery.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was in the declining period of mourning for a relative and wished on the seventh day of the seventh month to gather civil and military officials in the northern park for horse archery.

sentences.zh: 普惠奏記於澄曰：

translations.literal: Puhui submitted a memorial note to Cheng saying:
translations.idiomatic: Puhui submitted a memorial to Cheng saying:

sentences.zh: 竊聞三殺九親，別疏昵之敘；

translations.literal: I have heard that the three degrees of killing and the nine kinship categories distinguish the order of distant and close affection;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the three degrees of mourning and the nine kinship categories distinguish degrees of closeness in affection;

sentences.zh: 五服六術，等衰麻之心。

translations.literal: the five grades of mourning garments and six calculations equalize the heart of hempen grief.
translations.idiomatic: the five grades of mourning garments and six calculations regulate the heart's grief in hemp.

sentences.zh: 皆因事飾情，不易之道者也。

translations.literal: All are ways of adorning feeling according to circumstance—the unchanging Way.
translations.idiomatic: All of these adorn feeling according to circumstance; such is the unchanging Way.

sentences.zh: 然則莫大之痛，深於終身之外；

translations.literal: Thus the greatest pain extends deeper than the span of a lifetime;
translations.idiomatic: The greatest grief extends deeper than a single lifetime;

sentences.zh: 書策之哀，除于喪紀之內。

translations.literal: the grief recorded in writing and tally is removed within the period of mourning regulation.
translations.idiomatic: while the formal expression of mourning is confined within the period prescribed by ritual.

sentences.zh: 外者不可無節，故斷之以三年；

translations.literal: What is external cannot be without regulation, and so it is cut off at three years;
translations.idiomatic: Outward expression cannot be without limit, and so it is cut off at three years;

sentences.zh: 內者不可遂除，故敦之以日月。

translations.literal: what is internal cannot be promptly removed, and so it is urged on by months and days.
translations.idiomatic: but inward grief cannot be quickly dismissed, and so it is sustained through months and days.

sentences.zh: 況《禮》，大練之日，鼓素琴，蓋推以即吉也；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Rites, on the day of great refinement one drums on a plain zither—this is roughly pushing toward auspiciousness;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Rites prescribe that on the day of great refinement one may drum on a plain zither, which is roughly a move toward auspicious conduct;

sentences.zh: 小功以上，非虞祔練除不沐浴，此拘之以制也。

translations.literal: for lesser merit and above, unless at the services of reassurance, side-altar, and refinement one does not bathe—this is binding them with regulation.
translations.idiomatic: and for mourning above the lesser merit grade, one does not bathe except at the reassurance, side-altar, and refinement services—such is the binding force of ritual regulation.

sentences.zh: 曾子問曰：「相識有喪服，可以與於祭乎？」

translations.literal: Zengzi asked, "If one acquainted with the deceased is in mourning garments, may he take part in sacrifice?"
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi asked, "If one acquainted with the deceased is in mourning garments, may he take part in sacrifice?"

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「緦不祭，又何助於人。」

translations.literal: Confucius said, "One in the finest hemp does not sacrifice—how then could he help others?"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "One in the finest hemp mourning does not sacrifice—how then could he assist others?"

sentences.zh: 祭既不與，疑無宴食之道。

translations.literal: Since he does not take part in sacrifice, I suspect there is no way for feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Since such a person does not take part in sacrifice, I suspect there is no justification for feasting either.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「廢喪服，可以與於饋奠之事乎？」

translations.literal: He also said, "If one has cast off mourning garments, may he take part in presenting offerings at a funeral?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "If one has cast off mourning garments, may he take part in presenting offerings at a funeral?"

sentences.zh: 子曰：「脫衰與奠，非禮也。」

translations.literal: The Master said, "To remove the declining hemp and present offerings is not ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The Master said, "To remove the declining hemp mourning and present offerings is not ritual."

sentences.zh: 注云：「謂其忘哀疾。」

translations.literal: The commentary says, "This means forgetting grief too hastily."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, "This means forgetting grief too hastily."

sentences.zh: 愚謂除喪之始，不與饋奠，小功之內，其可觀射乎？

translations.literal: I venture to say that at the beginning of removing mourning one does not take part in presenting offerings—within the lesser merit period, can one watch archery?
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that at the beginning of removing mourning one does not present offerings—within the lesser merit period, can one watch archery?

sentences.zh: 《雜記》云：「大功以下，既葬適人，人食之。

translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Records say, "Below the greater merit grade, after burial when one visits another's home, the host may feed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Records say, "Below the greater merit grade, after burial when one visits another's home, the host may feed him.

sentences.zh: 其黨也食之，非其黨不食。」

translations.literal: If of his party they feed him; if not of his party they do not feed him."
translations.idiomatic: If he is of the host's party they feed him; if not of the host's party they do not feed him."

sentences.zh: 食猶擇人，于馬射為或非宜。

translations.literal: Even in eating one still chooses people—for horse archery this may perhaps be inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Even in eating one still chooses one's company—for horse archery this may perhaps be inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 伏見明教，立射會之限，將以二七令辰，集城中文武肄武藝於北園，行揖讓於中否。

translations.literal: I have seen the enlightened instruction setting a limit for the archery assembly, intending on the propitious day of the seventh of the seventh to gather civil and military officials within the city to drill martial arts in the northern park and perform bowing and yielding in the central pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen Your Grace's instruction setting a date for an archery assembly, intending on the seventh day of the seventh month to gather civil and military officials within the city to drill martial arts in the northern park and perform the rituals of bowing and yielding in the central pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時非大閱之秋，景涉妨農之節，國家縞禫甫除，殿下功衰仍襲，釋而為樂，以訓百姓，便是易先王之典教，忘哀戚之情，恐非所以昭令德、視子孫者也。

translations.literal: The season is not that of the great review; the occasion touches a time that hinders farming; the state has just removed its white and hempen mourning; Your Highness still wears the declining merit garments—to cast them off for pleasure and thereby instruct the common people would be to alter the canonical teachings of the former kings and forget the feelings of grief and sorrow; I fear this is not the way to display bright virtue and set an example for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: This is not the season for a grand military review, nor a time when farming should be interrupted; the state has only just laid aside its mourning garments, and Your Highness is still in the declining period of mourning—to set grief aside for pleasure and thereby instruct the people would be to overturn the canonical teachings of the former kings and forget the obligations of grief; I fear this is not how to display bright virtue or set an example for posterity.

sentences.zh: 案射儀，射者以禮樂為本，忘而從事，不可謂禮；

translations.literal: According to the archery rites, the archer takes ritual and music as his foundation; to forget them and pursue the activity cannot be called ritual;
translations.idiomatic: According to the archery rites, the archer takes ritual and music as his foundation; to forget them and pursue the activity cannot be called ritual;

sentences.zh: 鐘鼓弗設，不可謂樂。

translations.literal: if bells and drums are not set out, it cannot be called music.
translations.idiomatic: and if bells and drums are not set out, it cannot be called music.

sentences.zh: 舍此二事，何用射為！

translations.literal: Abandon these two matters—what use is archery!
translations.idiomatic: Without these two elements, what purpose does archery serve?

sentences.zh: 又七日之戲，令制無之，班勞所施，慮違事體，府庫空虛，宜待新調。

translations.literal: Moreover, the seventh-day diversions have no place in current regulations; the distribution of rewards for labor may violate the substance of affairs, and the treasury is empty—one ought to wait for new allocations.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the seventh-day diversions have no place in current regulations; distributing rewards for labor may violate propriety, and the treasury is empty—rewards should wait until new funds are allocated.

sentences.zh: 乞至九月，備飾盡行，然後奏《狸首》之章，宣矍相之命，聲軒縣，建雲鉦，神人忻暢于斯時也。

translations.literal: I beg that it be postponed until the ninth month, when preparations and ornaments are complete, and then perform the chapter of "Li Shou," proclaim the command of the archery master, sound the suspended bells, raise the cloud gongs, and let spirits and men rejoice at that time.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the assembly be postponed until the ninth month, when all preparations are complete, and then perform the "Li Shou" chapter, proclaim the archery master's command, sound the suspended bells, raise the cloud gongs, and let spirits and men rejoice together.

sentences.zh: 澄意納其言，託辭自罷，乃答曰：「今雖非公制，而此州承前已有斯式。

translations.literal: Cheng was inclined to accept his words and, using an excuse, called off the event himself; he then replied, "Though this is not now a public regulation, this province has inherited the practice from earlier times.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was inclined to accept his argument and, using an excuse, called off the event himself; he then replied, "Though this is not now a public regulation, this province has inherited the practice from earlier times.

sentences.zh: 且纂文習武，人之常藝。

translations.literal: Moreover, compiling texts and practicing martial arts are the ordinary skills of men.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, literary study and martial training are ordinary human pursuits.

sentences.zh: 豈可于常藝之間，要須令制乎？

translations.literal: How can one insist on imperial regulations for ordinary skills?
translations.idiomatic: Must one insist on imperial regulations for ordinary skills?

sentences.zh: 《禮》，兄弟內除，明哀已殺；

translations.literal: The Rites say that between brothers internal mourning is removed, showing that grief has been diminished;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say that between brothers internal mourning is removed, showing that grief has been diminished;

sentences.zh: 小功，客至主不絕樂。

translations.literal: for lesser merit, when a guest arrives the host does not cease music.
translations.idiomatic: and for lesser merit mourning, when a guest arrives the host does not cease music.

sentences.zh: 聽樂則可，觀武豈傷？

translations.literal: To listen to music is permissible—how could watching martial displays be harmful?
translations.idiomatic: If listening to music is permissible, how could watching martial displays be harmful?

sentences.zh: 直自事緣須罷，先以令停，方獲此請，深具來意。」

translations.literal: It is simply that circumstances require cancellation; I have already ordered a halt by command and have now obtained this request—I deeply appreciate your intent."
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that circumstances require cancellation; I have already ordered a halt by command and have now obtained your request—I deeply appreciate your intent."

sentences.zh: 澄轉揚州，啟普惠以羽林監領鎮南大將軍開府主簿。

translations.literal: Cheng was transferred to Yang province and recommended Puhui as supervisor of the Palace Guard, concurrently chief clerk of the Southern Pacification Grand General's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng was transferred to Yang province, he recommended Puhui as supervisor of the Palace Guard with concurrent appointment as chief clerk of the Southern Pacification Grand General's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 普惠既為澄知，曆佐二籓，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: Puhui, having been known to Cheng, served as aide in two princely establishments and gained considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Having won Cheng's confidence, Puhui served as aide in two princely establishments and gained considerable reputation.

sentences.zh: 還朝，仍羽林監。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he continued as supervisor of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he continued as supervisor of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 澄遭太妃憂，臣僚為立碑頌，題碑欲云「康王元妃之碑」。

translations.literal: When Cheng suffered mourning for the grand consort, his officials proposed erecting a stele inscription and wished to inscribe it "Stele of the Primary Consort of Prince Kang."
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng entered mourning for the grand consort, his officials proposed erecting a commemorative stele and wished to inscribe it "Stele of the Primary Consort of Prince Kang."

sentences.zh: 澄訪于普惠，普惠答曰：「謹尋朝典，但有王妃，而無元字。

translations.literal: Cheng consulted Puhui, who replied, "Carefully examining court regulations, there is only 'princely consort' and no character yuan for 'primary.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng consulted Puhui, who replied, "Carefully examining court regulations, there is only 'princely consort' and no character yuan meaning 'primary.

sentences.zh: 魯夫人孟子稱元妃者，欲下與繼室聲子相對。

translations.literal: When Lady Meng of Lu called herself primary consort, she wished to set herself below and opposite to the successor consort Lady Shengzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Meng of Lu called herself primary consort, she wished to distinguish herself from the successor consort Lady Shengzi.

sentences.zh: 今烈懿太妃作配先王，更無聲子、仲子之嫌，竊謂不假元字以別名位。

translations.literal: Now the Lieyi grand consort was matched to the former king, and there is no longer the taint of Shengzi or Zhongzi; I venture to say there is no need to borrow the character yuan to distinguish name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Lieyi grand consort was matched to the former king, and there is no longer any question of successor consorts; I venture to say there is no need for the character yuan to distinguish her rank.

sentences.zh: 且以氏配姓，愚以為在生之稱，故《春秋》'夫人姜氏至自齊'；

translations.literal: Moreover, pairing clan name with surname—I consider this a designation for the living; thus the Spring and Autumn Annals records 'Lady Jiang arrived from Qi';
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, pairing clan name with surname is, I believe, a designation for the living; thus the Spring and Autumn Annals records 'Lady Jiang arrived from Qi';

sentences.zh: 既葬，以諡配姓，故經書'葬我小君文薑'，又曰'來歸夫人成風之襚'，皆以諡配姓。

translations.literal: after burial, posthumous name is paired with surname; thus the classic records 'We buried our lesser lord Wen Jiang' and also says 'The lady returned with the funeral gifts of Cheng Feng'—all pair posthumous name with surname.
translations.idiomatic: after burial, posthumous name is paired with surname; thus the classic records 'We buried our lesser lord Wen Jiang' and also says 'The lady returned with the funeral gifts of Cheng Feng'—all pair posthumous name with surname.

sentences.zh: 古者婦人從夫諡，今烈懿太妃德冠一世，故特蒙褒錫，乃萬代之高事，豈容於定名之重，而不稱 '烈懿'乎。」

translations.literal: In antiquity women followed their husbands in posthumous names; now the Lieyi grand consort's virtue crowned the age, and she was specially granted praise—this is a matter of high honor for ten thousand generations; how can one, in the weight of fixing her name, fail to use 'Lieyi'?"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity women followed their husbands in posthumous names; now the Lieyi grand consort's virtue crowned the age, and she was specially honored—this is a matter of the highest dignity for ten thousand generations; how can one, in fixing her name, fail to use 'Lieyi'?"

sentences.zh: 澄從之。

translations.literal: Cheng followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 後為步兵校尉，以本官領河南尹丞。

translations.literal: Later he became commandant of foot soldiers and concurrently served as assistant to the Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became commandant of foot soldiers and concurrently served as assistant to the Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 宣武崩，坐與甄楷等飲酒遊從，免官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, he was punished for drinking and roaming in company with Zhen Kai and others and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, he was punished for drinking and roaming in company with Zhen Kai and others and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 故事，免官者，三載之後，降一階而敘，若才優擢授，不拘此限。

translations.literal: By precedent, those dismissed from office, after three years, are reappointed one rank lower; if talent is outstanding they may be promoted without regard to this limit.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, those dismissed from office are reappointed one rank lower after three years; if talent is outstanding they may be promoted without regard to this limit.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，吏部尚書李韶奏普惠有文學。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era, Li Shao, director of the Ministry of Personnel, memorialized that Puhui possessed literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era, Li Shao, director of the Ministry of Personnel, memorialized that Puhui possessed literary learning.

sentences.zh: 依才優之例，敕除甯遠將軍、司空倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: According to the precedent for outstanding talent, an edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distant and staff officer in the storehouse bureau of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: According to the precedent for outstanding talent, an edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distant and staff officer in the storehouse bureau of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 朝議以不降階為榮。

translations.literal: Court discussion regarded it as an honor that he was not demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion regarded it as an honor that he was not demoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 時任城王澄為司空，表議書記多出普惠。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Cheng of Ren-city was Minister of Works, and most memorials and deliberative documents came from Puhui's hand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Cheng of Ren-city was Minister of Works, and most memorials and deliberative documents came from Puhui's hand.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王恭、北海王顥疑為所生祖母服期與三年，詔群僚會議。

translations.literal: Princes Gong of Guangling and Hao of Beihai questioned whether mourning for their biological grandmothers should be one year or three years; an edict ordered the assembled officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Gong of Guangling and Hao of Beihai questioned whether mourning for their biological grandmothers should be one year or three years; an edict ordered the assembled officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 普惠議曰：

translations.literal: Puhui argued:
translations.idiomatic: Puhui argued:

sentences.zh: 謹案：二王祖母皆受命先朝，為二國太妃，可謂受命于天子，為始封之母矣。

translations.literal: Carefully examining the case: both princes' grandmothers received their appointments from the former court and became grand consorts of two states—they may be said to have received appointment from the Son of Heaven and to have been mothers at the time of initial enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Carefully examining the case: both princes' grandmothers received their appointments from the former court and became grand consorts of two states—they may be said to have received appointment from the Son of Heaven and to have been mothers at the time of initial enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》「慈母如母」，在三年章，傳曰：「貴父命也。」

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments state that 'a nurturing mother is like a mother' in the three-year section; the commentary says, 'This honors the father's command.'
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments state that 'a nurturing mother is like a mother' in the three-year section; the commentary says, 'This honors the father's command.'

sentences.zh: 鄭注云：「大夫之妾子，父在為母大功，則士之妾子為母期。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says, 'The son of a great officer's concubine, while the father lives, wears greater merit for the mother; then the son of a servitor's concubine wears one year for the mother.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says, 'The son of a great officer's concubine, while the father lives, wears greater merit mourning for the mother; the son of a servitor's concubine wears one year for the mother.

sentences.zh: 父卒，則皆得伸。」

translations.literal: When the father dies, both may extend mourning."
translations.idiomatic: When the father dies, both may extend mourning to three years."

sentences.zh: 此大夫命其妾子，以為母所慈，猶曰貴父命，為之三年；

translations.literal: This is the great officer commanding his concubine's son, whom the mother cherished—still it is said to honor the father's command and wear three years;
translations.idiomatic: This is the great officer commanding his concubine's son, whom the mother cherished—still it is said to honor the father's command and wear three years;

sentences.zh: 況天子命其子為列國王，命其所生母為國太妃，反自同公子為母練冠之與大功乎。

translations.literal: how much more when the Son of Heaven commands his son to be king of a feudal state and commands the son's biological mother to be grand consort of the state—can one instead equate them with an heir who wears dyed cap and greater merit for his mother?
translations.idiomatic: how much more when the Son of Heaven commands his son to be king of a feudal state and commands the son's biological mother to be grand consort of the state—can one instead equate them with an heir who wears dyed cap and greater merit mourning for his mother?

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「始封之君，不臣諸父昆弟。」

translations.literal: The commentary says, 'The lord at initial enfeoffment does not treat paternal uncles and brothers as subjects."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, 'The lord at initial enfeoffment does not treat paternal uncles and brothers as subjects."

sentences.zh: 則當服其親服。

translations.literal: Then one ought to wear the mourning of close kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Then one ought to wear the mourning of close kinship.

sentences.zh: 若魯、衛列國，相為服期，判無疑矣。

translations.literal: If Lu and Wei were feudal states mourning each other for one year, there would be no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If Lu and Wei were feudal states mourning each other for one year, there would be no doubt.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this made clear?
translations.idiomatic: How is this made clear?

sentences.zh: 《喪服》：「君為姑姊妹女子子嫁于國君者。」

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments: 'The lord wears mourning for paternal aunts, sisters, and daughters married to feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments: 'The lord wears mourning for paternal aunts, sisters, and daughters married to feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「何以大功？

translations.literal: The commentary says, 'Why greater merit?
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, 'Why greater merit mourning?

sentences.zh: 尊同也。

translations.literal: Equal in honor.
translations.idiomatic: Equal in honor.

sentences.zh: 尊同，則得服其親服。

translations.literal: Equal in honor, then one may wear the mourning of close kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Equal in honor, then one may wear the mourning of close kinship.

sentences.zh: 諸侯之子稱公子，公子不得禰先君。」

translations.literal: The son of a feudal lord is called heir; the heir may not enshrine the former lord as his own."
translations.idiomatic: The son of a feudal lord is called heir; the heir may not enshrine the former lord as his own ancestor."

sentences.zh: 然則兄弟一體，位列諸侯，自以尊同，得相為服，不可還准公子，遠厭天王。

translations.literal: Thus brothers are one body, both ranked as feudal lords; by equal honor they may mourn each other—they cannot be referred back to the heir standard and distantly suppress the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thus brothers are one body, both ranked as feudal lords; by equal honor they may mourn each other—they cannot be referred back to the heir standard and distantly suppress the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故降有四品，君、大夫以尊降，公子、大夫之子以厭降，名例不同，何可亂也。

translations.literal: Therefore reduction has four grades: lord and great officer reduce by honor; heir and great officer's son reduce by suppression—the categories differ in name; how can they be confused?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore reduction has four grades: lord and great officer reduce by honor; heir and great officer's son reduce by suppression—the categories differ in name; how can they be confused?

sentences.zh: 《禮》，大夫之妾子，以父命慈己，申其三年。

translations.literal: The Rites: the great officer's concubine's son, when the father commands that the mother cherish him, extends mourning to three years.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites: the great officer's concubine's son, when the father commands that the mother cherish him, extends mourning to three years.

sentences.zh: 太妃既受命先帝，光昭一國，二王胙土茅社，顯錫大邦，舍尊同之高據，附不禰之公子，雖許、蔡失位，亦不是過。

translations.literal: The grand consort having received appointment from the former emperor and shining over a state, the two princes receiving altars of earth and spirits of grain and bright grants of great domains—to abandon the high ground of equal honor and attach to the heir who cannot enshrine his ancestor would be excessive even for Xu and Cai losing their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The grand consort having received appointment from the former emperor and shining over a state, the two princes receiving altars of earth and spirits of grain and bright grants of great domains—to abandon the high ground of equal honor and attach to the heir who cannot enshrine his ancestor would be excessive even for Xu and Cai losing their positions.

sentences.zh: 《服問》曰：「有從輕而重，公子之妻，為其皇姑。」

translations.literal: Questions on Mourning Garments says, 'There is going from light to heavy: the heir's wife mourns for her imperial aunt-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Questions on Mourning Garments says, 'There is going from light to heavy: the heir's wife mourns for her imperial aunt-in-law."

sentences.zh: 公子雖厭，妻尚獲申，況廣陵、北海，論封君則封君之子，語妃則命妃之孫，承妃纂重，遠別先皇，更以先後之正統，厭其所生之祖嫡，方之皇姑，不以遙乎？

translations.literal: Though the heir is suppressed, his wife may still extend mourning—how much more for Guangling and Beihai: speaking of the enfeoffed lord, they are sons of enfeoffed lords; speaking of the consort, they are grandsons of the appointed consort; they inherit the consort's heavy succession, far separated from the former emperor, yet further use the orthodox line of primary and secondary to suppress the primary grandmother who bore them—compared with the imperial aunt-in-law, is this not more distant?
translations.idiomatic: Though the heir is suppressed, his wife may still extend mourning—how much more for Guangling and Beihai: speaking of the enfeoffed lord, they are sons of enfeoffed lords; speaking of the consort, they are grandsons of the appointed consort; they inherit the consort's heavy succession, far separated from the former emperor, yet further use the orthodox line of primary and secondary to suppress the primary grandmother who bore them—compared with the imperial aunt-in-law, is this not more distant?

sentences.zh: 今既許其申服，而復限之以期，比之慈母，不亦爽歟？

translations.literal: Now having permitted them to extend mourning yet again limiting them to one year—compared with the nurturing mother, is this not inconsistent?
translations.idiomatic: Now having permitted them to extend mourning yet again limiting them to one year—compared with the nurturing mother, is this not inconsistent?

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「為君之祖父母、父母、妻、長子」，《傳》曰：「何以期？

translations.literal: The classic says, 'For the lord's grandparents, parents, wife, and eldest son,' and the commentary says, 'Why one year?
translations.idiomatic: The classic says, 'For the lord's grandparents, parents, wife, and eldest son,' and the commentary says, 'Why one year?

sentences.zh: 父母長子君服斬。

translations.literal: For parents and eldest son the lord wears cutting hemp.
translations.idiomatic: For parents and eldest son the lord wears cutting hemp.

sentences.zh: 妻則小君。

translations.literal: The wife is the lesser lord.
translations.idiomatic: The wife is the lesser lord.

sentences.zh: 父卒，然後為祖後者，服斬。」

translations.literal: When the father dies, then the successor to the grandfather wears cutting hemp."
translations.idiomatic: When the father dies, then the successor to the grandfather wears cutting hemp."

sentences.zh: 今祖乃獻文皇帝，諸侯不得祖之。

translations.literal: Now the grandfather is Emperor Xianwen; feudal lords may not treat him as grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Now the grandfather is Emperor Xianwen; feudal lords may not treat him as grandfather.

sentences.zh: 母為太妃，蓋二王三年之證。

translations.literal: The mother as grand consort is roughly proof of the two princes' three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The mother as grand consort is proof of the two princes' three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 議者近背正經，以附非類，差之毫毛，所失或遠。

translations.literal: The debaters nearly betray the correct classic to attach to improper categories—a hair's breadth of difference may lead to vast error.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters nearly betray the correct classic to attach to improper categories—a hair's breadth of difference may lead to vast error.

sentences.zh: 且天子尊則配天，莫非臣妾，何為命之為國母，而不聽子服其親乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Son of Heaven is honored he is matched with Heaven—all are his subjects and concubines; why command one as mother of the state yet not allow the son to mourn his close kin?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the Son of Heaven is honored he is matched with Heaven—all are his subjects; why command one as mother of the state yet not allow the son to mourn his close kin?

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「從服者，所從亡則已。」

translations.literal: The Record says, 'For dependent mourning, when the one followed is gone it ceases."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, 'For dependent mourning, when the one followed is gone it ceases."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「不為君母之黨服，則為其母之黨服。」

translations.literal: It also says, 'If one does not mourn for the lord mother's party, then one mourns for one's own mother's party.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 'If one does not mourn for the lord mother's party, then one mourns for one's own mother's party.'

sentences.zh: 今所從既亡，不以親服服其所生，則屬從之服，于何所施？

translations.literal: Now the one followed is already gone; if one does not wear close kin mourning for the one who bore one, then to whom is dependent mourning applied?
translations.idiomatic: Now the one followed is already gone; if one does not wear close kin mourning for the one who bore one, then to whom is dependent mourning applied?

sentences.zh: 若以諸王入為公卿，便同大夫者，則當今之議皆不須以國為言也。

translations.literal: If because princes enter service as high ministers they are equated with great officers, then in today's debate there is no need to speak in terms of states at all.
translations.idiomatic: If because princes enter service as high ministers they are equated with great officers, then in today's debate there is no need to speak in terms of states at all.

sentences.zh: 今之諸王，自同列國，雖不之國，別置臣僚，玉食一方，得不以諸侯言之？

translations.literal: Today's princes are themselves equal to feudal states; though they do not go to their states, they separately appoint officials and enjoy jade food in a region—can one fail to speak of them as feudal lords?
translations.idiomatic: Today's princes are themselves equal to feudal states; though they do not go to their states, they separately appoint officials and enjoy princely sustenance in a region—can one fail to speak of them as feudal lords?

sentences.zh: 敢據《周禮》，輒同三年。

translations.literal: I venture to rely on the Rites of Zhou and propose three years alike.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to rely on the Rites of Zhou and propose three years alike.

sentences.zh: 當時議者，亦有同異。

translations.literal: Among the debaters at the time there were also agreements and differences.
translations.idiomatic: Among the debaters at the time there were also agreements and differences.

sentences.zh: 國子博士李郁于議罷之後，書難普惠，普惠據《禮》還答，鄭重三反，郁議遂屈。

translations.literal: Li Yu, academician of the Imperial University, after the debate ended wrote to challenge Puhui; Puhui replied on the basis of the Rites, solemnly three times, and Yu's argument was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, academician of the Imperial University, after the debate ended wrote to challenge Puhui; Puhui replied on the basis of the Rites, solemnly three times, and Yu's argument was defeated.

sentences.zh: 轉諫議大夫，澄謂普惠曰：「不喜君得諫議，唯喜諫議得君。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor; Cheng said to Puhui, "I am not pleased that you obtained the censorate—only pleased that the censorate obtained you."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to censor; Cheng said to Puhui, "I am not pleased that you obtained the censorate—only pleased that the censorate obtained you."

sentences.zh: 時靈太后父司徒胡國珍薨，贈相國、太上秦公。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Ling's father, Minister of Works Hu Guozhen, died; he was posthumously awarded Chancellor of State and Supreme Lord of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Ling's father, Minister of Works Hu Guozhen, died; he was posthumously awarded Chancellor of State and Supreme Lord of Qin.

sentences.zh: 普惠以前世後父無太上之號，詣闕上疏，陳其不可。

translations.literal: Puhui, because in former ages stepfathers had no title of Supreme, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial stating that this was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui, because in former ages stepfathers had no title of Supreme, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial stating that this was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 左右畏懼，莫敢為通。

translations.literal: Those around were afraid and none dared transmit it.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him were afraid and none dared transmit it.

sentences.zh: 會聞胡家穿壙下墳有磐石，乃密表曰：「竊見故侍中、司徒胡公，懷道含靈，實誕聖後，近樞克惟允之寄，居槐體論道之明。

translations.literal: It happened that he heard that when the Hu family dug the tomb chamber a boulder was found below the grave; he then submitted a secret memorial saying, "I have seen the late attendant within the gates and Minister of Works Lord Hu, who embraced the Way and contained spirit, truly begetting the sage descendant; near the pivot he fulfilled the trust of sincerity, in the locust hall he embodied the clarity of discussing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that he heard that when the Hu family dug the tomb chamber a boulder was found below the grave; he then submitted a secret memorial saying, "I have seen the late attendant within the gates and Minister of Works Lord Hu, who embraced the Way and contained spirit, truly begetting the sage descendant; near the pivot he fulfilled the trust of sincerity, in the locust hall he embodied the clarity of discussing the Way.

sentences.zh: 故以功餘九錫，褒假鸞纛，深聖上之加隆，極慈後之至愛，憲章天下，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Therefore with merit beyond the nine bestowals, praise and loan of imperial banners, deeply the sage sovereign's added elevation, utmost the compassionate empress's supreme love—establishing regulations for all under Heaven, is this not permissible!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with merit beyond the nine bestowals, praise and loan of imperial banners, deeply the sage sovereign's added elevation, utmost the compassionate empress's supreme love—establishing regulations for all under Heaven, is this not permissible!

sentences.zh: 而太上之號，竊謂未衷。

translations.literal: Yet the title of Supreme—I venture to say it is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the title of Supreme—I venture to say it is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰：'天無二日，土無二王，嘗禘郊社，尊無二上。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: 'Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings; at the seasonal sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain, honor has no second above.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says: 'Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings; at the seasonal sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain, honor has no second above.'

sentences.zh: '竊謂高祖受禪于獻文皇帝，故仰尊為太上皇，此因上上而生名也。

translations.literal: I venture to say that Emperor Gaozu received the abdication from Emperor Xianwen and therefore looked up to honor him as Supreme Emperor—this name arose from having one above another.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that Emperor Gaozu received the abdication from Emperor Xianwen and therefore looked up to honor him as Supreme Emperor—this name arose from having one sovereign above another.

sentences.zh: 皇太后稱令以系敕下，蓋取三從之道，遠同文母，列於十亂，則司徒為太上，恐乖系敕之意。

translations.literal: The empress dowager uses the title of command to tie edicts downward—this roughly takes the way of the three followings, far matching Mother Wen, listed among the ten disruptors; then for the Minister of Works to be Supreme perhaps violates the intent of tying edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager uses the title of command to tie edicts downward—this roughly takes the way of the three followings, far matching Mother Wen, listed among the ten disruptors; then for the Minister of Works to be Supreme perhaps violates the intent of tying edicts.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰'困於上者，必反於下。

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'One trapped above must turn back below.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'One trapped above must turn back below.'

sentences.zh: '比克吉定兆，而以淺改卜，群心悲惋，亦或天地神靈所以垂至戒，啟聖情。

translations.literal: Now having determined the auspicious omen yet changing the divination because the site is shallow, the hearts of the multitude grieve—perhaps Heaven and Earth and the spirits therefore bestow the utmost warning to awaken sage feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Now having determined the auspicious omen yet changing the divination because the site is shallow, the hearts of the multitude grieve—perhaps Heaven and Earth and the spirits therefore bestow the utmost warning to awaken sage feeling.

sentences.zh: 伏願停司徒逼同之號，從卑下不逾之稱，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I bow and wish that the forced equivalent title for the Minister of Works be stopped and that a humble designation not exceeding propriety be followed—then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I bow and wish that the forced equivalent title for the Minister of Works be stopped and that a humble designation not exceeding propriety be followed—then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 太后覽表，親至國珍宅，召集五品已上博議其事。

translations.literal: The empress dowager read the memorial and personally went to Guozhen's residence, summoning those of fifth rank and above to debate the matter broadly.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager read the memorial and personally went to Guozhen's residence, summoning those of fifth rank and above to debate the matter broadly.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄、太傅清河王懌、侍中崔光、御史中尉元匡、尚書崔亮並同有難，普惠並以理正之，無所屈。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Ren-city, Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe, attendant within the gates Cui Guang, censor Yuan Kuang, and director Cui Liang all similarly raised objections; Puhui corrected them all with reason and none prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Ren-city, Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe, attendant within the gates Cui Guang, censor Yuan Kuang, and director Cui Liang all similarly raised objections; Puhui corrected them all with reason and none prevailed.

sentences.zh: 廷尉少卿袁翻曰：「《周官》：上公九命，上大夫四命，命數雖殊，同名為上，何必上者皆是極尊。」

translations.literal: Yuan Fan, vice director of the Court of Justice, said, "The Offices of Zhou: the highest duke has nine commands, the highest great officer four commands—though the numbers of commands differ, both are named 'upper'; why must 'upper' always mean supreme honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fan, vice director of the Court of Justice, said, "The Offices of Zhou: the highest duke has nine commands, the highest great officer four commands—though the numbers of commands differ, both are named 'upper'; why must 'upper' always mean supreme honor?"

sentences.zh: 普惠厲聲呵翻曰：「禮有下卿、上士，何止大夫與公。

translations.literal: Puhui sternly shouted at Fan, "The Rites have lower minister and upper servitor—how limited to great officer and duke!
translations.idiomatic: Puhui sternly shouted at Fan, "The Rites have lower minister and upper servitor—how limited to great officer and duke!

sentences.zh: 但今所行，乙太加上，二名雙舉，不得非極。

translations.literal: But what is now practiced adds Supreme above—two names raised together cannot but be supreme.
translations.idiomatic: But what is now practiced adds Supreme above—two names raised together cannot but be supreme.

sentences.zh: 雕蟲小藝，微或相許，至於此處，豈卿所及！」

translations.literal: Petty ornamental arts—one might slightly concede—but as to this point, is it within your reach!"
translations.idiomatic: Petty ornamental arts—one might slightly concede—but as to this point, is it within your reach!"

sentences.zh: 翻甚有慚色，默不復言。

translations.literal: Fan was deeply ashamed in countenance and silently spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was deeply ashamed and silently spoke no more.

sentences.zh: 議者咸以太后當朝，志相黨順，遂奏曰：「張普惠辭雖不屈，然非臣等所同。

translations.literal: The debaters all thought that with the empress dowager holding court, their wills aligned in partisan compliance; they then memorialized, "Zhang Puhui's words, though not yielding, are not what we agree with.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters all thought that with the empress dowager holding court, their wills aligned in partisan compliance; they then memorialized, "Zhang Puhui's words, though not yielding, are not what we agree with.

sentences.zh: 渙汗已流，請依前詔。」

translations.literal: The edict has already been issued in full—we request following the previous decree."
translations.idiomatic: The edict has already been issued in full—we request following the previous decree."

sentences.zh: 太后復遣元叉、賈璨宣令謂普惠曰：「朕之所行，孝子之志；

translations.literal: The empress dowager again sent Yuan Cha and Jia Can to proclaim the command to Puhui, saying, "What We do is the will of a filial child;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager again sent Yuan Cha and Jia Can to proclaim the command to Puhui, saying, "What We do is the will of a filial child;

sentences.zh: 卿之所陳，忠臣之道。

translations.literal: what you state is the way of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: what you state is the way of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 群公已有成議，卿不得苦奪朕懷。

translations.literal: The assembled lords already have a settled decision—you must not bitterly wrest Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled lords already have a settled decision—you must not bitterly wrest Our mind.

sentences.zh: 後有所見，勿得難言。」

translations.literal: If hereafter you have views, do not speak difficult words."
translations.idiomatic: If hereafter you have views, do not speak difficult words."

sentences.zh: 初，普惠被召，傳詔馳驊騮馬來，甚迅速，佇立催去。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Puhui was summoned, the edict-transmitter came on a piebald horse, very swiftly; he stood waiting and urged departure.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Puhui was summoned, the edict-transmitter came on a piebald horse, very swiftly; he stood waiting and urged departure.

sentences.zh: 普惠諸子憂怖涕泗。

translations.literal: Puhui's sons were anxious and fearful, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui's sons were anxious and fearful, weeping.

sentences.zh: 普惠謂曰：「我當休明之朝，掌諫議之任，若不言所難言，諫所難諫，便是唯唯，曠官屍祿。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "I serve in a brilliant and enlightened age and hold the office of remonstrator. If I do not speak what is hard to speak and remonstrate where remonstrance is hard, I would merely nod assent—neglecting my office while drawing salary.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui said, "I serve a brilliant age in the office of remonstrator. If I fail to speak the unspeakable and remonstrate where remonstrance is perilous, I am no better than one who nods along—holding a post in name only while living off the state's pay.

sentences.zh: 人生有死，死得其所，夫復何恨。

translations.literal: A man's life ends in death; if death comes in its proper place, what regret remains?
translations.idiomatic: Every life must end; if one dies where duty calls, what room is there for regret?

sentences.zh: 然朝廷有道，汝輩勿憂。」

translations.literal: Yet the court follows the Way—you need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: The court still holds to the Way. You need not worry.

sentences.zh: 及議罷，旨勞還宅，親故賀其幸甚。

translations.literal: When the deliberation ended, an edict commended him and sent him home; relatives and friends congratulated him on his great good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended, an edict commended him and sent him home. Relatives and friends congratulated him on his extraordinary good fortune.

sentences.zh: 時中山杜弼遺書普惠曰：「明侯深儒碩學，身負大才，執此公方，來居諫職，謇謇如也，諤諤如也。

translations.literal: At that time Du Bi of Zhongshan sent a letter to Puhui saying: "Your Excellency is a deeply learned Confucian scholar, bearing great talent. Holding to this impartial integrity, you have taken up the office of remonstrator—upright indeed, boldly outspoken indeed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Bi of Zhongshan wrote to Puhui: "Your Excellency is a scholar of profound learning and great talent. With such impartial integrity you have taken up the remonstrator's post—steadfast in principle, fearless in speech.

sentences.zh: 一昨承在胡司徒弟，當庭面諍，雖問難鋒至，而應對響出。

translations.literal: The day before yesterday I learned that at the residence of Hu Guozhen, Minister of Works, you remonstrated face-to-face in court. Though the challenges came sharp as blades, your replies rang out like echoes.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday I heard that at Minister of Works Hu Guozhen's residence you remonstrated to his face in open court. Though the cross-examination cut like a blade, your answers rang back clear and swift.

sentences.zh: 宋城之帶始縈，魯門之柝裁警，終使群後逡巡，庶僚拱默。

translations.literal: The sash of Songcheng was just being girded, the watch-clapper at Lu Gate had scarcely sounded—at last the high ministers hesitated and the lesser officials stood silent with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: Like the girding of the sash at Songcheng, like the first alarm at Lu Gate—you made the great ministers hang back and the whole assembly fall silent.

sentences.zh: 雖不見用於一時，固已傳美於百代。

translations.literal: Though not employed at the time, your fame will surely be transmitted through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Though your counsel was not taken then, your renown will endure for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 聞風快然，敬裁此白。」

translations.literal: Hearing of this I was greatly pleased; respectfully I compose this note.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted to hear of it, I respectfully send this brief letter.

sentences.zh: 普惠美其此書，每為口實。

translations.literal: Puhui praised this letter and often cited it in conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui admired the letter and often quoted it afterward.

sentences.zh: 普惠以天下人調，幅度長廣，尚書計奏，復徵綿麻，恐人不堪命。

translations.literal: Puhui, because corvée levies on the people nationwide had grown broad and long in measure and the Ministry submitted calculations calling again for hemp and silk levies, feared the people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui saw that corvée levies across the realm had grown ever broader and heavier, and when the Ministry calculated and memorialized to restore the hemp-and-silk tax, he feared the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「伏聞尚書奏復綿麻之調，遵先皇之軌。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant humbly hears that the Ministry has memorialized restoring the hemp-and-silk levy, following the former emperor's track.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial that read: "I humbly learn that the Ministry has proposed restoring the hemp-and-silk levy in accord with the former emperor's precedent.

sentences.zh: 夙宵惟度，欣戰交集。

translations.literal: From early morning to late night I have pondered this; joy and trepidation interweave.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I have weighed the matter, my heart torn between hope and fear.

sentences.zh: 仰惟高祖廢大鬥，去長尺，改重秤，所以愛萬姓，從薄賦。

translations.literal: Looking up, I consider that Emperor Gaozu abolished the large bushel, removed the extended foot-rule, and altered the heavy steelyard—all to cherish the myriad people and follow light taxation.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that Emperor Gaozu abolished the oversized bushel, shortened the extended foot-rule, and lightened the heavy steelyard—all to show care for the people and keep taxes low.

sentences.zh: 知軍國須綿麻之用，故云幅度之間，億兆應有綿麻之利，故絹上稅綿八兩，布上稅麻十五斤。

translations.literal: Knowing that army and state required hemp and silk, he said that within the measures of cloth breadth and length the hundred million ought to yield hemp and silk profit; hence on silk cloth tax eight liang of floss, on hemp cloth tax fifteen jin of hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that army and state still needed hemp and silk, he held that within the standard measures of cloth the people could afford such levies—eight liang of floss on each bolt of silk, fifteen jin of hemp on each bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 萬姓得廢大鬥，去長尺，改重秤，荷輕賦之饒，不適於綿麻而已。

translations.literal: The myriad people gained abolition of the large bushel, removal of the long foot, and alteration of the heavy steelyard—they received the bounty of light taxation, not limited to hemp and silk alone.
translations.idiomatic: The people gained relief from oversized measures and heavy weights and enjoyed the bounty of lighter taxes—not in hemp and silk alone, but in every levy.

sentences.zh: 故歌舞以供其賦，奔走以役其勤。

translations.literal: Hence they sang and danced to supply their levies and ran about to fulfill their labor service.
translations.idiomatic: They sang as they paid their taxes and hurried willingly to their corvée duties.

sentences.zh: 夫信行於上，則億兆樂輸於下。

translations.literal: When trust is practiced above, the hundred million below gladly submit their taxes.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne keeps faith, the people pay their dues with goodwill.

sentences.zh: 自茲已降，漸漸長闊，百姓嗟怨，聞於朝野。

translations.literal: From then downward it gradually grew broader and longer; the people's sighs of resentment were heard at court and in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the burdens have steadily widened and deepened, until the people's complaints resounded through court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太后未臨朝之前，陛下居諒暗之日，宰輔不尋其本，知天下之怨綿麻，不察其幅廣、度長、秤重、鬥大，革其所弊，存其可存，而特放綿麻之調，以悅天下之心。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly considers that before Empress Dowager Ling took the regency, when Your Majesty was in mourning seclusion, the chief ministers did not seek out the root cause. Knowing the realm resented the hemp-and-silk levy, they did not examine the broad cloth measures, long foot-rules, heavy steelyards, and large bushels—reforming what was corrupt and keeping what could be kept—but merely released the hemp-and-silk levy alone to please the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that before Empress Dowager Ling assumed the regency, while Your Majesty was still in mourning seclusion, the chief ministers never traced the problem to its root. They knew the realm resented the hemp-and-silk tax, yet instead of correcting the inflated measures—the broad cloth widths, long foot-rules, heavy steelyards, and oversized bushels—they merely abolished the hemp-and-silk levy alone, hoping thereby to win the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 此謂悅之不以道，愚臣所以未悅者也。」

translations.literal: This is what is called pleasing people not by the Way—why your foolish servant is not pleased."
translations.idiomatic: That is pleasing the people without following the Way—and that is why this humble servant cannot rejoice."

sentences.zh: 普惠又表乞朝直之日，時聽奉見。

translations.literal: Puhui again memorialized requesting that on days of court duty he be allowed audience at times.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui memorialized again, asking that on his days of court attendance he be granted regular audiences.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，月一陛見。

translations.literal: From then on he had one monthly audience at the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was granted one audience at the palace steps each month.

sentences.zh: 又以孝明不親視朝，過崇佛法，郊廟之事，多委有司，上疏曰：「伏惟陛下重暉纂統，欽明文思，天地屬心，百神佇望。

translations.literal: Also, because Emperor Xiaoming did not personally preside at court and excessively honored Buddhist Law, leaving suburban and temple rites mostly to the responsible officials, he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant humbly considers that Your Majesty has succeeded to the radiance doubly bright, reverently continuing civil and literary brilliance—Heaven and Earth look to you, the hundred spirits wait in hope.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Emperor Xiaoming no longer presided at court in person, honored Buddhism to excess, and left most suburban and temple rites to subordinates. He submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has inherited a doubly radiant throne and carries forward a civil and literary legacy. Heaven and Earth look to you; the hundred spirits await your lead.

sentences.zh: 伏願躬致郊廟之虔，親紆朔望之澤，釋奠成均，竭心千畝，明發不寐，潔誠禋祼，孝弟可以通神明，德教可以光四海。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes that Your Majesty personally perform the devotions at the suburban and temple altars, personally extend the blessings of the new and full moon, offer the libation at the Imperial Academy, devote heart to the thousand-mu field, rise at dawn without sleep, and with pure sincerity perform the burnt and libation offerings—filial piety and brotherliness can reach the divine intelligences, and moral teaching can shine over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will personally perform the rites at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, personally grant the blessings of the new and full moon, offer the libation at the Imperial Academy, devote yourself to the sacred plowing field, rise before dawn in sleepless devotion, and with pure sincerity perform the burnt and libation offerings—for filial piety and brotherly duty can reach the spirits, and moral teaching can illuminate the four seas.

sentences.zh: 然後精進三寶，信心如來。

translations.literal: Only then advance diligently in the Three Treasures and place faith in the Tathāgata.
translations.idiomatic: Only then should you advance in the Three Treasures and place your faith in the Tathāgata.

sentences.zh: 道由化深，故諸漏可盡；

translations.literal: The Way, through deepening transformation, can thus exhaust all outflows;
translations.idiomatic: Through deepening cultivation the Way can drain away every defilement;

sentences.zh: 法隨禮積，故彼岸可登。

translations.literal: the Law, accumulated along with ritual, can thus bring one to the other shore.
translations.idiomatic: and through the accumulation of ritual and Law one can reach the farther shore.

sentences.zh: 量撤僧寺不急之華，還復百官久折之秩。

translations.literal: Measure and withdraw the non-urgent splendors of Buddhist temples, and restore the ranks long withheld from the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Trim the needless extravagance of Buddhist temples and restore the salaries long withheld from the officials.

sentences.zh: 已興之構，務從簡成；

translations.literal: Works already begun should be completed as simply as possible;
translations.idiomatic: Projects already under way should be finished as modestly as possible;

sentences.zh: 將來之造，權令停息。

translations.literal: future construction should for now be halted.
