translations.idiomatic: and new construction should be suspended for the time being.

sentences.zh: 但仍舊貫，亦何必改作。

translations.literal: Yet follow the old practices—why must there be change for change's sake?
translations.idiomatic: Where old ways still serve, there is no need to alter them for alteration's sake.

sentences.zh: 庶節用愛人，法俗俱賴。」

translations.literal: Thus economy in expenditure and care for people may be relied upon by both Law and custom.
translations.idiomatic: In this way thrift and care for the people may benefit both the Buddhist order and the civil realm.

sentences.zh: 尋別敕付外，議釋奠之禮。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward a separate edict was issued to the outer offices to discuss the rites of the libation offering.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a separate edict was sent to the outer offices to deliberate the rites of the libation offering.

sentences.zh: 時史官克日蝕，豫敕罷朝。

translations.literal: At that time the historiographers fixed a date for an eclipse and an advance edict canceled court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the historiographers calculated the date of an eclipse, and an advance edict canceled court.

sentences.zh: 普惠以逆廢非禮，上疏陳之。

translations.literal: Puhui held that canceling court in advance was against ritual and submitted a memorial stating this.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui held that canceling court preemptively violated ritual propriety and submitted a memorial explaining why.

sentences.zh: 又表論時政得失：一曰審法度，平鬥尺，租調務輕，賦役務省。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on the gains and losses of current governance: First, examine measures and standards, equalize bushels and foot-rules; keep land and corvée levies light and labor service minimal.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial on the strengths and failings of current policy. First: scrutinize standards of measure, restore fair bushels and foot-rules, keep land taxes and corvée levies as light as possible, and reduce labor service to the minimum.

sentences.zh: 二曰聽輿言，察怨訟，先皇舊事有不便於政者，請悉追改。

translations.literal: Second, heed cart and well talk, investigate grievances and lawsuits; where former emperor's old measures are inconvenient to governance, please fully revise them.
translations.idiomatic: Second: heed what people say in the streets, investigate grievances and lawsuits, and revise every former emperor's policy that no longer serves good governance.

sentences.zh: 三曰進忠謇，退不肖，任賢勿貳，去邪勿疑。

translations.literal: Third, advance the loyal and outspoken, remove the unworthy; employ the worthy without wavering, eliminate the corrupt without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Third: promote the loyal and outspoken, dismiss the unworthy, appoint the capable without second thoughts, and remove the corrupt without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 四曰興滅國，繼絕世，勳親之胤，所宜收敘。

translations.literal: Fourth, restore extinguished states and continue severed lineages; descendants of meritorious kin should be gathered and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: restore extinguished houses and continue broken lineages—the descendants of meritorious kin ought to be gathered and given their due.

sentences.zh: 書奏，孝明、靈太后引普惠于宣光殿，隨事難詰。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xiaoming and Empress Dowager Ling summoned Puhui to Xuanguang Hall and pressed him with difficult questions on each point.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Xiaoming and Empress Dowager Ling summoned Puhui to Xuanguang Hall and questioned him closely on each point.

sentences.zh: 延對移時，太后曰：「小小細務，一一翻動，更成煩擾。」

translations.literal: The extended audience lasted a long time. The Empress Dowager said: "Petty minor matters, stirring up each one—this only creates further vexation.
translations.idiomatic: The audience dragged on for a long while. The Empress Dowager said, "These are trifling matters. To stir up each one only creates more trouble.

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「聖上之養庶物，若慈母之養赤子。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "The sage sovereign nourishes the myriad people as a loving mother nourishes her infant.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui replied, "The sage sovereign nourishes the people as a loving mother nourishes her infant.

sentences.zh: 今赤子幾臨危壑，將赴水火，以煩勞而不救，豈赤子所望于慈母！」

translations.literal: Now the infant nearly faces a perilous ravine and is about to fall into fire and water—if the mother does not save him for fear of trouble, is this what the infant expects of a loving mother!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that infant stands at the edge of a chasm, about to fall into fire and water—if the mother refuses to save him for fear of trouble, is that what an infant expects of its mother?"

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「天下蒼生，寧有如此苦事？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "The common people under Heaven—can there really be such suffering?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Can the people of the realm truly suffer so grievously?"

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「天下之親懿，莫重于太師彭城王，然遂不免枉死。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "Among those close and honored under Heaven, none was weightier than Grand Tutor the Prince of Pengcheng—yet he still could not escape wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui said, "Of all those honored and close to the throne, none ranked higher than Grand Tutor the Prince of Pengcheng—yet even he died unjustly.

sentences.zh: 微細之苦，何可得無？」

translations.literal: How could there be no suffering among the humble and lowly?"
translations.idiomatic: How then can the humble and lowly be free of suffering?"

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「彭城之苦，吾已封其三子，何足復言。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "As for the Prince of Pengcheng's suffering, I have already enfeoffed his three sons—what need to speak of it again?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "As for the Prince of Pengcheng, I have already enfeoffed his three sons. There is no need to speak of it again."

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「聖後封彭城之三子，天下莫不忻至德，知慈母之在上。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "When the sage empress enfeoffed the Prince of Pengcheng's three sons, none under Heaven failed to rejoice at supreme virtue, knowing a loving mother was above.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui said, "When Your Majesty enfeoffed the Prince of Pengcheng's three sons, all under Heaven rejoiced at your supreme virtue and knew a loving mother sat upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣所以重陳者，凡如此枉，乞垂聖察。」

translations.literal: Your servant repeats this because every such wrong—your servant begs you to extend sagely scrutiny."
translations.idiomatic: I raise the matter again because every such injustice, I beg, deserves your sagely attention."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿雲興滅繼絕，意復誰是？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "You spoke of restoring extinguished states and continuing severed lineages—whom do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "You spoke of restoring extinguished houses and continuing broken lineages—whom do you have in mind?"

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「昔淮南逆終，漢文封其四子，蓋骨肉之不可棄，親親故也。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "In former times when the Prince of Huainan's rebellion ended, Emperor Wen of Han enfeoffed his four sons—bone and flesh must not be cast aside; that is the principle of cherishing kin.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui said, "When the Prince of Huainan's rebellion ended, Emperor Wen of Han enfeoffed his four sons—for bone and flesh must not be cast aside. That is the principle of cherishing one's kin.

sentences.zh: 竊見咸陽、京兆，乃皇子皇孫，一德之虧，自貽悔戾；

translations.literal: I have observed that the Princes of Xianyang and Jingzhao were imperial sons and grandsons; one lapse in virtue brought regret and offense upon themselves;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the Princes of Xianyang and Jingzhao were imperial sons and grandsons. A single lapse in virtue brought ruin upon themselves;

sentences.zh: 沈淪幽壤，緬焉弗收，豈是興滅繼絕之意？」

translations.literal: sunk in the dark earth, far away with no restoration—is this the intent of restoring the extinguished and continuing the severed?"
translations.idiomatic: yet they lie buried in darkness, their lines left unrestored—is that the meaning of restoring the fallen and continuing the broken?"

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿言有理，當命公卿博議。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Your words have reason; I shall order the grand ministers to debate broadly."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Your argument has merit. I shall order the grand ministers to deliberate the matter fully."

sentences.zh: 及任城王澄薨，普惠荷其恩待，朔望奔赴，至於禫除，雖寒暑風雨，無不必至。

translations.literal: When Prince Cheng of Ren-city died, Puhui bore his grace and favor; on the first and fifteenth of each month he hastened to attend, until the end of mourning—through cold and heat, wind and rain, he never failed to come.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Cheng of Ren-city died, Puhui, deeply indebted to his kindness, attended on the first and fifteenth of every month through the full mourning period. Through heat and cold, wind and rain, he never missed a visit.

sentences.zh: 初，澄嘉賞普惠，臨薨啟為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At first Cheng greatly admired Puhui; on his deathbed he recommended him as Right Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cheng had greatly admired Puhui, and on his deathbed recommended him for appointment as Right Vice Director of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 靈太后既深悼澄，覽啟從之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, deeply mourning Cheng, read the recommendation and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, grieving deeply for Cheng, read the recommendation and approved it.

sentences.zh: 詔行之後，尚書諸郎以普惠地寒，不應便居管轄，相與為約，並欲不放上省，紛紜多日乃息。

translations.literal: After the edict was issued, the various clerks of the Ministry felt Puhui's background was humble and he ought not immediately hold supervisory rank; they made a pact together and all refused to let him enter the Ministry—a tumult that lasted many days before subsiding.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was issued, the Ministry clerks held that Puhui's family background was too lowly for immediate supervisory office. They made a pact among themselves and refused to admit him to the Ministry—a dispute that raged for many days before it subsided.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，詔遣楊鈞送蠕蠕主阿那瑰還國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang, an edict dispatched Yang Jun to escort Ana Gui, lord of the Ruanruan, back to his country.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang, an edict ordered Yang Jun to escort Ana Gui, lord of the Ruanruan, back to his homeland.

sentences.zh: 普惠謂遣之將貽後患，上疏極言其不可。

translations.literal: Puhui held that sending him back would bring future troubles and submitted a memorial strongly arguing against it.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui warned that sending him back would invite future disaster and submitted a memorial arguing forcefully against the plan.

sentences.zh: 表奏不從。

translations.literal: The memorial was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 魏子建為益州刺史，有贓罪，普惠被使驗之，事遂得釋，故子建父子甚德之。

translations.literal: Wei Zijian served as governor of Yizhou and had a corruption offense; Puhui was sent to investigate, and the matter was finally cleared—therefore Zijian father and son deeply owed him gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zijian, governor of Yizhou, was charged with corruption, Puhui was sent to investigate the case and secured his exoneration. Zijian and his son were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 時梁西豐侯正德詐稱降款，朝廷頗事當迎。

translations.literal: At the time the Marquis of Xifeng of Liang, Zheng De, falsely claimed surrender; the court made considerable preparations to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng De, Marquis of Xifeng in Liang, feigned surrender, and the court began making elaborate preparations to receive him.

sentences.zh: 普惠請付揚州，移還蕭氏，不從。

translations.literal: Puhui requested handing him to Yang Province to be returned to the Xiao clan—the request was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui asked that he be handed over to Yang Province and sent back to the Xiao house. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而正德果逃還。

translations.literal: Before long Zheng De indeed fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zheng De did indeed flee back.

sentences.zh: 後除光祿大夫，右丞如故。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, retaining his vice directorship.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness while retaining his post as vice director.

sentences.zh: 先是，仇池武興郡氐數反，西垂郡戍，租連久絕。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Di people of Wuxing Commandery in Qiuchi had repeatedly rebelled; the garrisons of the western frontier had long gone without continuous tax delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Di of Wuxing Commandery in Qiuchi had rebelled repeatedly, and tax deliveries to the western frontier garrisons had long ceased.

sentences.zh: 詔普惠以本官為持節、西道行台，給秦、岐、涇、華、雍、豳、東秦七州兵武三萬人，任其召發；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Puhui, in his existing office, as Commissioner with the Staff and Western Circuit Mobile Office, supplying thirty thousand troops from the seven provinces of Qin, Qi, Jing, Hua, Yong, Bin, and Eastern Qin, with authority to mobilize as he saw fit;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Puhui, retaining his existing rank, as Commissioner with the Staff and head of the Western Circuit Mobile Office, with thirty thousand troops from Qin, Qi, Jing, Hua, Yong, Bin, and Eastern Qin at his disposal and authority to mobilize them as needed;

sentences.zh: 送南秦、東益二州兵租，分付諸戍。

translations.literal: and dispatching military provisions from Southern Qin and Eastern Yizhou to distribute among the garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: and with orders to deliver military provisions from Southern Qin and Eastern Yizhou and distribute them among the garrisons.

sentences.zh: 其所部將統，聽于關西牧守之中隨機召遣。

translations.literal: The generals and commanders under his command might be summoned and dispatched at discretion from among the pastoral and guarding officials west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and commanders under his command might be drawn at need from among the governors and guard officials west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 軍資板印之屬，悉以自隨。

translations.literal: Military supplies, seals on boards, and the like—all were to accompany him personally.
translations.idiomatic: Military supplies, official seals, and the like were all placed at his personal disposal.

sentences.zh: 事訖還朝，賜絹布一百段。

translations.literal: When the mission was completed he returned to court and was granted one hundred rolls of silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission was finished he returned to court and was rewarded with one hundred bolts of silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 時詔訪冤屈，普惠上疏，多所陳論。

translations.literal: When an edict sought cases of wrongful punishment, Puhui submitted memorials with many arguments.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for reports of wrongful punishment, Puhui submitted memorials setting forth many cases.

sentences.zh: 出除東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed governor of Eastern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out and appointed governor of Eastern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南九戍十三郡，猶因梁前弊，別郡異縣之人錯雜居止。

translations.literal: The nine garrisons and thirteen commanderies of the Huainan region still suffered from former Liang abuses—people from different commanderies and counties lived mixed together.
translations.idiomatic: In the nine garrisons and thirteen commanderies of Huainan, the old disorders of Liang rule still lingered, with people from different commanderies and counties living jumbled together.

sentences.zh: 普惠乃依次括比，省減郡縣，上表陳狀，詔許之。

translations.literal: Puhui then registered and compared them in order, reduced commanderies and counties, submitted a memorial stating the facts, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui then conducted a systematic census, consolidated and reduced commanderies and counties, submitted a memorial detailing the changes, and received imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 宰守因此，綰攝有方，奸盜不起，人以為便。

translations.literal: Because of this the magistrates and guard officials had proper control—bandits and thieves did not arise, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and guard officials were thereby able to govern effectively. Banditry ceased, and the people found the new arrangement a great improvement.

sentences.zh: 普惠不營財業，好有進舉，敦於故舊。

translations.literal: Puhui did not pursue wealth; he liked to advance worthy people and was devoted to old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui did not pursue wealth. He delighted in promoting worthy people and was steadfast toward old friends.

sentences.zh: 冀州人侯堅固少時與其遊學，早終。

translations.literal: Hou Jiangu of Jizhou had traveled and studied with him in youth and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jiangu of Jizhou had been his companion in travel and study in youth, but died young.

sentences.zh: 其子長瑜，普惠每於四時請祿，無不減贍，給其衣食。

translations.literal: His son Changyu—each season Puhui would request salary and never failed to provide generously, supplying his food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changyu—each season Puhui would set aside part of his salary and never failed to provide for him, supplying food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 及為豫州，啟長瑜解褐，攜其合門拯給之。

translations.literal: When he became governor of Yuzhou, he recommended Changyu for initial office and brought his whole household under his relief and support.
translations.idiomatic: When he became governor of Yuzhou, he recommended Changyu for his first official appointment and took in his entire household, providing for them all.

sentences.zh: 在州卒，諡曰宣恭。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Xiangong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously titled Xiangong, "Sincere and Respectful."

sentences.zh: 成淹，字季文，上谷居庸人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Yan, style name Jiwen, was a man of Juyong in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yan, courtesy name Jiwen, was from Juyong in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 好文學，有氣尚。

translations.literal: He loved literature and had a vigorous, principled spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature and possessed a spirited, principled character.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為員外郎，領軍主，援東陽、曆城。

translations.literal: He served Song as external clerk and garrison commander, reinforcing Dongyang and Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Song as an external clerk and garrison commander, reinforcing Dongyang and Licheng.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，降慕容白曜，赴闕，授兼著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era he surrendered to Murong Baiyao, went to the capital, and was appointed acting Assistant Director in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangxing era he surrendered to Murong Baiyao, went to the capital, and was appointed acting Assistant Director in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 時獻文于仲冬月欲巡漠北，朝臣以寒甚固諫，並不納。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xianwen wished in the mid-winter month to tour the northern deserts; court ministers firmly remonstrated because of the extreme cold—all were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xianwen planned a mid-winter tour of the northern deserts. The court ministers remonstrated firmly against it because of the bitter cold, but none of their counsel was accepted.

sentences.zh: 淹上《接輿釋遊論》，帝覽之，詔尚書李䐶曰：「卿諸人不如成淹論，通釋人意。」

translations.literal: Yan submitted "Jie Yu's Explanation of Wandering"; the Emperor read it and issued an edict Minister Li Shen: "You all are not equal to Cheng Yan's essay—it thoroughly explains what people mean.
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted his "Jie Yu's Explanation of Wandering." The Emperor read it and said to Minister Li Shen, "None of you match Cheng Yan's essay—it gets to the heart of what people mean.

sentences.zh: 乃敕停行。

translations.literal: An edict then halted the tour.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued canceling the tour.

sentences.zh: 太和中，文明太后崩，齊遣其散騎常侍裴昭明、散騎侍郎謝竣等來吊，欲以朝服行事。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Empress Dowager Wenming died; Qi sent Attendant Cavalier Pei Zhaoming, Attendant Cavalier Xie Jun, and others to offer condolences, wishing to perform the rites in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era, after Empress Dowager Wenming died, Qi sent Attendant Cavalier Pei Zhaoming, Attendant Cavalier Xie Jun, and others to offer condolences, intending to perform the rites in court dress.

sentences.zh: 主客不許，昭明等執志不移。

translations.literal: The host officials did not permit it; Zhaoming and the others held to their intent without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: The host officials refused, but Zhaoming and his party would not yield.

sentences.zh: 孝文敕尚書李沖選一學識者更與論執。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict Minister Li Chong to select a learned man to debate the matter further with them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen ordered Minister Li Chong to choose a learned scholar to debate the matter with them further.

sentences.zh: 沖奏遣淹。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized recommending Yan be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Chong memorialized recommending Yan for the task.

sentences.zh: 昭明言：「不聽朝服行禮，義出何典？」

translations.literal: Zhaoming said: "Not allowing mourning rites in court dress—on what canonical authority does this rule rest?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said, "If court dress may not be worn for mourning rites, on what canonical authority does that rule rest?

sentences.zh: 淹言：「玄冠不吊，童孺共聞。

translations.literal: Yan said: "The black cap is not worn for condolence visits—even children have heard this.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "The black cap is not worn for condolence visits—even children know that.

sentences.zh: 昔季孫將行，請遭喪之禮，千載之下，猶共稱之。

translations.literal: In former times when Ji Sun was about to depart, he requested the rites for encountering mourning; a thousand years later people still praise him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jisun was about to set out on a journey, he asked to observe the rites for encountering mourning—and a thousand years later people still praise him for it.

sentences.zh: 卿方謂義出何典，何其異哉！」

translations.literal: You now ask on what canonical authority this rests—how strange!"
translations.idiomatic: And you ask me on what canonical authority this rests—how extraordinary!"

sentences.zh: 昭明言：「齊高帝崩，魏遣李彪通吊，初不素服，齊朝亦不為疑。」

translations.literal: Zhaoming said: "When Emperor Gaodi of Qi died, Wei sent Li Biao to offer condolences; he did not wear unadorned mourning dress at first, and the Qi court raised no objection."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said, "When Emperor Gaodi of Qi died, Wei sent Li Biao to offer condolences. He did not wear unadorned mourning dress, and the Qi court raised no objection."

sentences.zh: 淹言：「彪通吊之日，朝命以吊服自隨。

translations.literal: Yan said: "On the day Li Biao went to offer condolences, the court ordered mourning dress to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "On the day Li Biao went to offer condolences, the court ordered him to bring mourning dress with him.

sentences.zh: 彼不遵高宗追遠之慕，乃逾月即吉。

translations.literal: They did not follow Gaozong's yearning to honor the distant past, but ended mourning after just over a month.
translations.idiomatic: They did not observe Gaozong's example of honoring the departed, but ended mourning after little more than a month.

sentences.zh: 齊之君臣，皆已鳴玉盈庭，彪行人，何容獨以衰服間衣冠之中？

translations.literal: The ruler and ministers of Qi already fill the court with jade-clinking court dress—Li Biao as envoy, how could he alone wear sackcloth among robes and caps?
translations.idiomatic: The ruler and ministers of Qi already fill the court in full court dress with jade at their belts—how could Envoy Li Biao alone wear mourning sackcloth among them?

sentences.zh: 我皇處諒暗以來，百官聽於塚宰，卿豈得以此方彼也？」

translations.literal: Since our emperor has been in mourning seclusion, all officials defer to the chief minister—how can you compare this with that?"
translations.idiomatic: Since our emperor entered mourning seclusion, all officials have deferred to the chief minister—how can you set this case beside that one?"

sentences.zh: 昭明乃搖膝而言曰：「三皇不同禮，亦安知得失所歸。」

translations.literal: Zhaoming then swayed his knee and said: "The Three Sovereigns had different rites—how can one know where right and wrong lie?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming shifted in his seat and said, "The Three Sovereigns observed different rites—who can say where right and wrong truly lie?"

sentences.zh: 淹言：「若如來談，卿以虞舜、高宗為非也？」

translations.literal: Yan said: "If what you say is so, then you deem Yu Shun and Gaozong wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "If that is what you mean, then you hold Yu Shun and Gaozong to be in the wrong?"

sentences.zh: 昭明相顧笑曰：「非孝者，宣尼有成責，行人亦弗敢言。

translations.literal: Zhaoming exchanged glances and smiled: "As for unfilial conduct, Confucius has fixed rebuke—an envoy would not dare speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming exchanged glances with his companions and smiled. "On the question of unfilial conduct, Confucius has already pronounced judgment—an envoy would hardly dare speak of it.

sentences.zh: 使人唯齎袴褶，不可以吊，幸借衣颻，以申國命。

translations.literal: Our envoys brought only jacket and trousers and cannot offer condolences—we beg to borrow mourning garments to fulfill the state's commission.
translations.idiomatic: Our envoys brought only riding jacket and trousers and cannot properly offer condolences. We beg you to lend us mourning dress so that we may carry out our state's commission.

sentences.zh: 今為魏朝所逼，還南日，必得罪本朝。」

translations.literal: Now pressed by the Wei court, when we return south we will surely offend our own court."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Wei court has forced this upon us, when we return south we are sure to offend our own court."

sentences.zh: 淹言：「彼有君子也，卿將命折中，還南日，應有高賞。

translations.literal: Yan said: "If they have a gentleman there, you carried out your mission with compromise—when you return south you should receive great reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "If your court has men of principle, you carried out your mission with reasonable compromise—when you return south you should receive a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 若無君子也，但令有光國之譽，雖非理得罪，亦復何嫌。

translations.literal: If there is no gentleman, so long as you gain glory for your state, even if punished unreasonably, what is there to regret?
translations.idiomatic: If there are no such men, so long as you bring honor to your state, even if you are punished without cause, what is there to regret?

sentences.zh: 南史、董狐，自當直筆。」

translations.literal: The Southern History and Dong Hu will surely write with a straight brush."
translations.idiomatic: The historians of the south and men like Dong Hu will surely set down the truth without fear."

sentences.zh: 既而敕送衣颻給昭明等，明旦引入，皆令文武盡哀。

translations.literal: An edict then sent mourning garments to Zhaoming and the others; next morning they were brought in and all civil and military officials were made to mourn fully.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued sending mourning dress to Zhaoming and his party. The next morning they were admitted to court, and all civil and military officials were required to observe full mourning.

sentences.zh: 後正佐郎。

translations.literal: Later he was made Regular Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Regular Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 其後，齊遣其散騎常侍庾蓽、散騎侍郎何憲、主書邢宗慶等來聘，孝文敕淹接於外館。

translations.literal: Subsequently Qi sent Attendant Cavalier Yu Bi, Attendant Cavalier He Xian, Master of Documents Xing Zongqing, and others on a friendly mission; Emperor Xiaowen ordered Yan to receive them at the outer guesthouse.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Qi sent Attendant Cavalier Yu Bi, Attendant Cavalier He Xian, Master of Documents Xing Zongqing, and others on a diplomatic visit, and Emperor Xiaowen ordered Yan to receive them at the outer guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 宗慶語淹言：「南北連和既久，而比棄信絕好，為利而動，豈是大國善鄰之義？」

translations.literal: Zongqing said to Yan: "North and south have been allied for long, yet lately you broke faith and severed friendship, moved by profit—is this the way a great state treats a good neighbor?
translations.idiomatic: Zongqing said to Yan, "North and south have been at peace for a long time, yet recently you broke faith and cut off friendly relations, acting only for gain—is that how a great state honors good-neighbor relations?

sentences.zh: 淹言：「夫為王者不拘小節，豈得眷眷守尾生之信！

translations.literal: Yan said: "One who would be king does not cling to small points—how could one zealously keep Wei Sheng's punctilio of faith!
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "One who would be king does not bind himself to petty scruples—how could he cling stubbornly to Wei Sheng's rigid code of honor!

sentences.zh: 且齊先主曆事宋朝，當應便爾欺奪？」

translations.literal: Moreover Qi's founding lord served the Song dynasty for generations—would he simply seize and rob like that?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qi's founding lord served the Song dynasty for generations—would he simply have seized territory by fraud?"

sentences.zh: 宗慶、庾蓽及從者皆相顧失色。

translations.literal: Zongqing, Yu Bi, and their attendants all looked at one another, losing color.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqing, Yu Bi, and their attendants all looked at one another and turned pale.

sentences.zh: 何憲知淹昔從南入，以手掩目曰：「卿何不作于禁而作魯肅？」

translations.literal: He Xian, knowing Yan had once come from the south, covered his eyes with his hand and said: "Why make Lu Su instead of Yu Jin?
translations.idiomatic: He Xian, knowing Yan had once come from the south, covered his eyes with his hand and said, "Why play Lu Su when you ought to play Yu Jin?

sentences.zh: 淹言：「我舍逆效順，欲追蹤陳、韓，何于禁之有！」

translations.literal: Yan said: "I abandoned the rebellious and followed what is right, wishing to follow in the footsteps of Chen Ping and Han Xin—what Yu Jin is there in me!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "I abandoned the losing cause and followed what is right, hoping to follow in the footsteps of Chen Ping and Han Xin—what has that to do with Yu Jin!"

sentences.zh: 憲亦不對。

translations.literal: He did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: He Xian made no reply.

sentences.zh: 王肅之至，鑾輿行幸。

translations.literal: When Wang Su arrived, the imperial carriage set out on tour.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su arrived, the emperor set out on an imperial tour.

sentences.zh: 肅多扈從，敕淹將引，若有古跡，皆使知之。

translations.literal: Su often accompanied the retinue; an edict ordered Yan to serve as guide—wherever there were ancient sites, he was to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: Su often accompanied the imperial retinue, and an edict ordered Yan to serve as guide and inform him of every ancient site they passed.

sentences.zh: 行到朝歌，肅問：「此是何城？」

translations.literal: Reaching Chaoge, Su asked: "What city is this?
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Chaoge, Su asked, "What city is this?

sentences.zh: 淹言：「紂都朝歌城。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Chaoge, capital of King Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Chaoge, the capital of King Zhou of Shang."

sentences.zh: 肅言：「故應有殷之頑人。」

translations.literal: Su said: "So there ought to be the stubborn men of Yin still here."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Then there ought still to be the stubborn remnant people of Yin here."

sentences.zh: 淹言：「昔武王滅紂，悉居河洛，中因劉、石亂華，仍隨司馬東度。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "When King Wu destroyed Zhou, they all settled in the He-Luo region; midway due to the Liu and Shi disorder of China, they followed the Sima east across the river."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "When King Wu destroyed Zhou, they were all resettled in the He-Luo region. Later, during the chaos wrought by the Liu and Shi dynasties, they followed the Sima clan east across the river."

sentences.zh: 肅知淹寓青州，乃笑謂曰：「青州何必無其餘種。」

translations.literal: Su, knowing Yan had lived in Qingzhou, smiled and said: "Why should Qingzhou lack any remaining stock of them?"
translations.idiomatic: Su, knowing Yan had once lived in Qingzhou, smiled and said, "Why should Qingzhou be without its share of that remnant stock?"

sentences.zh: 淹以肅本隸徐州：「若言青州，本非其地，徐州間今日重來，非所知也。」

translations.literal: Yan, noting Su was originally from Xuzhou: "If you speak of Qingzhou, that is not your territory; as for Xuzhou—your people coming back today—I know nothing of that."
translations.idiomatic: Yan, noting that Su was originally from Xuzhou, replied, "If you speak of Qingzhou, that was never your home ground. As for Xuzhou and your people coming back today—I know nothing of that."

sentences.zh: 肅遂伏馬上掩口笑，顧謂侍御史張思甯曰：「向聊因戲言，遂致辭溺。」

translations.literal: Su then leaned on his horse covering his mouth laughing, turned to Attending Censor Zhang Sining and said: "Just now, a casual jest led to an outpouring of rhetoric."
translations.idiomatic: Su leaned over his saddle, covering his mouth as he laughed, and turned to Attending Censor Zhang Sining. "A passing jest just now drew forth far too much eloquence from him."

sentences.zh: 思甯馳馬以聞，孝文大悅，謂彭城王勰曰：「淹此段足為制勝。」

translations.literal: Sining galloped off to report; Emperor Xiaowen was greatly pleased and said to Prince Pengcheng Xie: "This exchange by Yan is enough to claim victory."
translations.idiomatic: Sining galloped ahead to report what had happened. Emperor Xiaowen was greatly pleased and said to Prince Pengcheng Xie, "In this exchange Yan more than held his own."

sentences.zh: 輿駕至洛，肅因侍宴，帝戲肅曰：「近者行次朝歌，聞成淹共卿殊有往復，卿試重敘之。」

translations.literal: When the imperial procession reached Luoyang, Su attended a banquet; the Emperor teased Su: "Recently at Chaoge I heard Cheng Yan had quite an exchange with you—try recounting it again."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession reached Luoyang, Su attended a banquet. The Emperor teased him, "On the recent stop at Chaoge I heard that Cheng Yan and you had quite a back-and-forth—try telling it again."

sentences.zh: 肅言：「臣於朝歌失言，一之已甚，豈宜再說。」

translations.literal: Su said: "Your servant misspoke at Chaoge—once was already too much; how could I tell it again?"
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Your servant misspoke at Chaoge. Once was already too much—how could I tell it again?"

sentences.zh: 遂大笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon great laughter.
translations.idiomatic: At that everyone burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 肅又言淹才詞，宜應敘進。

translations.literal: Su also spoke of Yan's literary talent and said he should be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Su also praised Yan's literary gifts and said he ought to be promoted.

sentences.zh: 帝言：「若因此進淹，恐辱卿轉甚。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If I promote Yan because of this, I fear it would humiliate you all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If I promote Yan because of this, I fear it would humiliate you all the more.

sentences.zh: 肅言：「臣屈己達人，正可顯臣之美。」

translations.literal: Su said: "Your servant humbles himself to advance others—that only displays my virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Your servant humbles himself to advance another—that only shows my virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿為人所屈，欲求屈己之名，復於卿大優。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You were bested by another, yet seek the name of self-abasement—that reflects even greater credit on you."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You were bested by another, yet you seek the reputation of self-abasement—that reflects even greater credit on you."

sentences.zh: 肅言：「淹既蒙進，臣得屈己申人，此所謂陛下惠而不費。」

translations.literal: Su said: "Since Yan receives promotion, your servant can abase himself and elevate another—this is what is called Your Majesty's bounty without cost."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Since Yan is to be promoted, your servant can humble himself and lift another up—this is what is called Your Majesty's bounty without cost."

sentences.zh: 遂酣笑而止。

translations.literal: They then laughed heartily and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They laughed heartily at that and let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 賜淹龍廄上馬一匹，並鞍勒宛具，朝服一襲。

translations.literal: Yan was granted a horse from the imperial stables, complete with saddle, bridle, and trappings, and one set of court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was granted a horse from the imperial stables, complete with saddle, bridle, and full trappings, and one set of court dress.

sentences.zh: 轉謁者僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Receptionists.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Director of the Palace Receptionists.

sentences.zh: 時遷都，帝以淹家貧，敕給事力，送至洛陽，使與家累相隨。

translations.literal: During the capital relocation, the Emperor, knowing Yan's family was poor, ordered servants supplied and sent him to Luoyang so his household could accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: During the move of the capital, the Emperor, knowing Yan's family was poor, ordered household servants provided and sent him on to Luoyang so that his family could accompany him.

sentences.zh: 及車駕濟淮，敕征淹。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage crossed the Huai, an edict summoned Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage crossed the Huai River, an edict summoned Yan.

sentences.zh: 淹于路左請見，曰：「敵不可小，願聖明保萬全之策。

translations.literal: Yan requested audience at the roadside and said: "The enemy must not be underestimated—I pray Your Sagely Wisdom will keep to a strategy of absolute safety.
translations.idiomatic: Yan requested an audience at the roadside and said, "The enemy must not be underestimated. I pray Your Sagely Wisdom will hold to a strategy of absolute safety.

sentences.zh: 伏聞發洛已來，諸有諫者，解官奪職，恐非聖明納下之義。」

translations.literal: I have heard that since departing Luoyang, all who remonstrated have been removed from office—which may not accord with the sage ruler's way of accepting counsel from below.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that since leaving Luoyang, every man who remonstrated has been dismissed from office. I fear that does not accord with a sage ruler's way of accepting counsel from below.

sentences.zh: 帝優而容之。

translations.literal: The Emperor treated him kindly and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received him graciously and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 帝幸徐州，敕淹與閭龍駒專主舟楫，將汎泗入河，溯流還洛。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Xuzhou and ordered Yan and Lu Longju to take exclusive charge of boats, intending to sail the Si into the Yellow River and return upstream to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited Xuzhou and ordered Yan and Lu Longju to take exclusive charge of the boats, intending to sail the Si River into the Yellow River and return upstream to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 軍次磝碻，淹以黃河浚急，慮有傾危，乃上疏陳諫。

translations.literal: The army halted at Qiaoque; Yan, because the Yellow River ran swift and deep, feared capsizing and submitted a memorial remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Qiaoque, Yan, fearing disaster because the Yellow River ran swift and deep, submitted a memorial remonstrating against the plan.

sentences.zh: 帝敕淹曰：「朕以恆、代無運漕之路，故京邑人貧。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict Yan: "Because Heng and Dai had no transport route for grain tribute, the capital district was poor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied to Yan, "Because Heng and Dai had no route for transporting grain tribute, the people of the capital district were poor.

sentences.zh: 今移都伊、洛，欲通運四方。

translations.literal: Now we relocate the capital to Yi and Luo, wishing to open transport to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we are moving the capital to Yi and Luo, I wish to open transport links to all four quarters.

sentences.zh: 黃河急浚，人皆難涉，我因此行乘流，所以開百姓之心。

translations.literal: The Yellow River runs swift and deep—all find it hard to cross. I take this journey riding the current precisely to open the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River runs swift and deep, and everyone finds it hard to cross. I am making this journey by riding the current precisely to open the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 知卿誠至而不得相納。」

translations.literal: I know your sincerity reaches the utmost, yet I cannot accept your counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I know your sincerity is complete, yet I cannot accept your counsel.

sentences.zh: 賜驊騮馬一匹，衣冠一襲。

translations.literal: He was granted a bay stallion and one set of robes and cap.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a bay stallion and one set of robes and cap.

sentences.zh: 除羽林監、主客令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and Director of Host Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and Director of Host Affairs.

sentences.zh: 于時宮殿初構，運材日有萬計。

translations.literal: At that time palace construction had just begun, and building timber transported daily numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At that time palace construction had just begun, and timber transported each day numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 伊、洛流澌，苦於厲涉。

translations.literal: The Yi and Luo ran with ice floes, making crossing painfully difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi and Luo rivers ran with ice floes, making crossing painfully difficult.

sentences.zh: 淹遂啟求敕都水造浮航。

translations.literal: Yan then petitioned requesting an edict for the Directorate of Waterways to build pontoon bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then petitioned for an edict ordering the Directorate of Waterways to build pontoon bridges.

sentences.zh: 帝賞納之，意欲榮淹於眾。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it, intending to honor Yan before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted the proposal, intending to honor Yan before the whole court.

sentences.zh: 朔旦受朝，百官在位，乃賜帛百匹，知左右二都水事。

translations.literal: On the first day of the month at court audience, with all officials in place, he granted a hundred bolts of silk and put him in charge of both Left and Right Directorates of Water Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the month at court audience, with all officials present, the Emperor granted him a hundred bolts of silk and put him in charge of both the Left and Right Directorates of Water Affairs.

sentences.zh: 景明三年，出除平陽太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingming he was sent out and appointed Administrator of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jingming era he was sent out and appointed Administrator of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 還朝，病卒，贈光州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he died of illness; posthumously awarded Governor of Guangzhou, posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court he died of illness. He was posthumously awarded the title Governor of Guangzhou and given the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子宵，字景鸞，好為文詠，坦率多鄙俗，與河東薑質等朋游相好，詩賦間起，知音之士所共嗤笑。

translations.literal: His son Xiao, style name Jingluan, loved composing verse; frank and often coarse, he formed friendships with Jiang Zhi of Hedong and others, occasionally producing poetry and rhapsodies—all of which connoisseurs mocked together.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiao, courtesy name Jingluan, loved composing verse. Frank and often coarse in manner, he formed close friendships with Jiang Zhi of Hedong and others and occasionally produced poetry and rhapsodies—all of which discerning readers mocked together.

sentences.zh: 卒于書侍御史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Attending Secretary in the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Attending Secretary in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 范紹，字始孫，燉氇皇龍勒人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shao, style name Shisun, was a man of Huanglongle in Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shao, courtesy name Shisun, was from Huanglongle in Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and quick.
translations.idiomatic: From an early age he was clever and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 年十二，父命就學，師事崔光。

translations.literal: At twelve his father ordered him to pursue study; he took Master Cui Guang as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of twelve his father ordered him to pursue his studies, and he took Master Cui Guang as his teacher.

sentences.zh: 以父憂廢業。

translations.literal: Due to mourning for his father he abandoned his studies.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he abandoned his studies.

sentences.zh: 母又誡之曰：「汝父卒日，令汝遠就崔生，稀有成立。

translations.literal: His mother admonished him: "On the day your father died he told you to go far to study under Master Cui, hoping you would achieve something.
translations.idiomatic: His mother admonished him, "On the day your father died he told you to go far away to study under Master Cui, hoping you would make something of yourself.

sentences.zh: 今已過期，宜遵成命。」

translations.literal: The mourning period has now passed—you should follow his final command.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning period has now passed. You should follow his final command.

sentences.zh: 紹還赴學。

translations.literal: Shao returned to his studies.
translations.idiomatic: Shao returned to his studies.

sentences.zh: 太和初，充太學生，轉算生，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he served as an imperial university student, then became a calendar student, and gained considerable exposure to the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he entered the imperial university, then became a calendar student, and gained a considerable grounding in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 孝文選為門下通事令史，遷錄事，掌奏文案。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen selected him as Clerk for General Affairs in the Secretariat, promoted him to Recorder, and put him in charge of memorial documents.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen selected him as Clerk for General Affairs in the Secretariat, then promoted him to Recorder and put him in charge of memorial documents.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，又為侍中李沖、黃門崔光所知。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought well of him; he was also recognized by Attendant Within Li Chong and Cui Guang of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought well of him, and he also won the recognition of Attendant Within Li Chong and Cui Guang of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝曾謂近臣曰：「崔光從容，範紹之力。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to close ministers: "Cui Guang provides the easy grace; Fan Shao provides the drive.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said to his close ministers, "Cui Guang supplies the easy grace; Fan Shao supplies the driving force.

sentences.zh: 後朝廷有南討計，發河北數州田兵，通緣淮戍兵合五萬餘人，廣開屯田。

translations.literal: Later when the court planned a southern campaign, farming soldiers from several Hebei provinces were mobilized; combined with garrison troops along the Huai totaling more than fifty thousand, they broadly opened military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the court planned a southern campaign, farming soldiers from several Hebei provinces were mobilized. Together with garrison troops stationed along the Huai, they numbered more than fifty thousand men, and military colonies were opened on a broad scale.

sentences.zh: 八座奏紹為西道六州營田大使，加步兵校尉。

translations.literal: The Eight Ministers memorialized appointing Shao Military Colony Commissioner for the six western-route provinces, with additional title Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers memorialized appointing Shao Military Colony Commissioner for the six provinces on the western route, with the additional title Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 紹勤於勸課，頻歲大獲。

translations.literal: Shao was diligent in encouraging cultivation; year after year harvests were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was diligent in encouraging cultivation, and year after year the harvests were abundant.

sentences.zh: 又詔與都督、中山王英論攻鐘離。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered him to discuss with the Area Commander, Prince Zhongshan Ying, the attack on Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered him to confer with the area commander, Prince Zhongshan Ying, on the attack on Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 紹觀其城隍，恐不可陷，勸令班師，英不從。

translations.literal: Shao observed its walls and moat and feared it could not be taken; he urged withdrawal but Ying would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao inspected the city's walls and moat and feared it could not be taken. He urged withdrawal, but Ying would not listen.

sentences.zh: 紹還，具以狀奏聞。

translations.literal: Shao returned and fully reported the situation in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shao returned and reported the full situation to the throne in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 俄而英敗。

translations.literal: Before long Ying was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ying was defeated.

sentences.zh: 後歷位并州刺史、太常卿。

translations.literal: Later he successively held posts as Governor of Bingzhou and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as Governor of Bingzhou and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he met his death at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 劉桃符，中山盧奴人也。

translations.literal: Liu Taofu was a man of Lunu in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taofu was from Lunu in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 生不識父，九歲喪母。

translations.literal: He never knew his father in life; at nine he lost his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He never knew his father in life, and at the age of nine he lost his mother.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，好學。

translations.literal: By nature deferential and careful, he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature deferential and careful, he loved learning.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，射策甲科。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he scored top class in the archery-and-policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he placed in the top class in the archery-and-policy examination.

sentences.zh: 曆碎職，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He passed through petty offices and was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through minor posts and was repeatedly promoted until he became a Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 以勤明見知，久不遷職。

translations.literal: Known for diligence and clarity, he went long without promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Known for diligence and clarity, he went for a long time without promotion.

sentences.zh: 宣武謂曰：「揚子雲為黃門，頓曆三世。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu said to him: "Yang Ziyun served at the Yellow Gate for three reigns in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu said to him, "Yang Ziyun served at the Yellow Gate through three reigns in succession.

sentences.zh: 卿居此任始十年，不足辭也。」

translations.literal: You have held this post for only ten years—it is too soon to decline.
translations.idiomatic: You have held this post for only ten years—it is too soon to ask to leave it.

sentences.zh: 東豫州刺史田益宗居邊貪穢，宣武頻詔桃符慰喻之。

translations.literal: Eastern Yuzhou Governor Tian Yizong on the frontier was greedy and corrupt; Emperor Xuanwu repeatedly issued an edict Taofu to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yuzhou Governor Tian Yizong, stationed on the frontier, was greedy and corrupt, and Emperor Xuanwu repeatedly ordered Taofu to go and counsel him.

sentences.zh: 桃符還，具稱益宗老耄，而諸子非理處物。

translations.literal: Taofu returned and fully reported that Yizong was old and senile while his sons handled affairs unreasonably.
translations.idiomatic: When Taofu returned, he reported fully that Yizong was old and senile while his sons handled affairs unreasonably.

sentences.zh: 宣武后欲代之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu afterward wished to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Emperor Xuanwu wished to replace him.

sentences.zh: 恐其背叛，拜桃符東豫州刺史，與後將軍李世哲領眾襲益宗。

translations.literal: Fearing rebellion, he appointed Taofu Governor of Eastern Yuzhou; with Rear General Li Shizhe he led troops to surprise Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing rebellion, he appointed Taofu Governor of Eastern Yuzhou and, together with Rear General Li Shizhe, led troops in a surprise attack on Yizong.

sentences.zh: 語在《益宗傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biography of Yizong.

sentences.zh: 桃符善恤蠻左，為人吏所懷。

translations.literal: Taofu was good at caring for the southern tribal populations and was beloved by officials and common people alike.
translations.idiomatic: Taofu was good at caring for the tribal peoples of the south and was beloved by officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 久之，徵還。

translations.literal: After long service he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After a long tenure he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 病卒，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He died of illness; posthumously awarded Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously awarded the title Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 鹿悆，字永吉，濟陰乘氏人也。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, style-name Yongji, was a man of Chenshi in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, courtesy name Yongji, was from Chenshi in Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 祖壽興，沮渠氏庫部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouxing was a Kubu-lang of the Juqu clan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shouxing had been a Kubu-lang of the Juqu clan.

sentences.zh: 父生，再為濟南太守，有政績。

translations.literal: His father Sheng twice served as Administrator of Jinan and had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng served twice as Administrator of Jinan and won a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 獻文嘉其能，特徵赴季秋馬射，賜以驄馬，加以青服，彰其廉潔。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen praised his ability, specially summoned him to the autumn horse-archery event, bestowed a piebald horse, added green robes, and displayed his integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen praised his ability and specially summoned him to the autumn horse-archery review, bestowing a piebald horse and green robes to honor his integrity and incorruptibility.

sentences.zh: 時三齊始附，人懷苟且，蒲博終朝，頗廢農業。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Qi had just submitted; people harbored lax attitudes, gambling all day, greatly neglecting agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Three Qi regions had only recently submitted; the people were given to lax ways, gambling from morning to night and greatly neglecting agriculture.

sentences.zh: 生立制斷之，聞者嗟善。

translations.literal: Sheng established regulations to prohibit it; those who heard sighed in approval.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng established regulations forbidding it, and those who heard of it sighed in approval.

sentences.zh: 後卒于淮陽太守，追贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he died while Administrator of Huaiyang; posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Administrator of Huaiyang and was posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 悆好兵書、陰陽、釋氏之學，彭城王勰召為館客。

translations.literal: Yu loved military texts, yin-yang studies, and Buddhist learning; Prince of Pengcheng Xie summoned him as a lodge guest.
translations.idiomatic: Yu loved military texts, yin-yang studies, and Buddhist learning, and Prince of Pengcheng Xie summoned him as a lodge guest.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣徐州，馬疲，附船而至大梁。

translations.literal: Once when going to Xuzhou his horse grew weary; he took a boat and arrived at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Once when traveling to Xuzhou his horse grew weary, so he took passage by boat and arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 夜睡，者上岸，竊禾四束飼馬。

translations.literal: At night while he slept, his attendant went ashore and stole four sheaves of grain to feed the horse.
translations.idiomatic: At night while he slept, his attendant went ashore and stole four sheaves of grain to feed the horse.

sentences.zh: 船行數里，悆覺，即停船至取禾處，以縑三丈置禾束下而反。

translations.literal: After the boat had gone several li, Yu noticed; he immediately stopped the boat, returned to where the grain had been taken, placed three zhang of silk beneath the sheaves, and went back.
translations.idiomatic: After the boat had gone several li, Yu noticed. He immediately stopped, returned to where the grain had been taken, placed three zhang of silk beneath the sheaves, and went back.

sentences.zh: 初為真定公子直國中尉，恆勸以忠廉之節。

translations.literal: At first he served as Commandant of the Principality for Zizhi, Prince of Zhending, and constantly exhorted him with the principles of loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Commandant of the Principality for Zizhi, Prince of Zhending, and constantly exhorted him to uphold loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 嘗賦五言詩曰：「嶧山萬丈樹，雕鏤作琵琶，由此材高遠，糸玄響藹中華。」

translations.literal: Once he composed a five-character poem saying: "A tree ten thousand zhang tall on Mount Yi, carved and inlaid to make a pipa—because its timber is lofty and far-reaching, its deep strings resound through the Central Lands."
translations.idiomatic: Once he composed a five-character poem that read: "A tree ten thousand zhang tall on Mount Yi, carved and inlaid to make a pipa—because its timber is lofty and far-reaching, its deep strings resound through the Central Lands."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「援琴起何調？

translations.literal: He also wrote: "When you draw the zither forth, what mode do you begin?
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "When you draw the zither forth, what mode do you begin?

sentences.zh: 幽蘭與白雪，絲管韻未成，莫使糸玄響絕！」

translations.literal: Orchid in Seclusion" and "White Snow"—the silk strings and pipes have not yet formed their harmony; do not let the deep strings' sound die away!"
translations.idiomatic: Orchid in Seclusion" and "White Snow"—the silk strings and pipes have not yet formed their harmony; do not let the deep strings' sound die away!"

sentences.zh: 子直少有令問，悆欲其善終，故以諷焉。

translations.literal: Zizhi had a fine reputation in youth; Yu wished him to end well, and so offered these verses as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi had a fine reputation in youth, and Yu wished him to finish well, so he offered these verses as admonition.

sentences.zh: 後隨子直鎮梁州，州有兵糧和糴，和糴者靡不潤屋，悆獨不取。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zizhi to garrison Liangzhou; the province had military grain he-di purchases—those involved in he-di all enriched their houses to overflowing, but Yu alone took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Zizhi to garrison Liangzhou. The province had military grain he-di purchases, and those who handled them all enriched their houses to overflowing, but Yu alone took nothing.

sentences.zh: 子直強之，終不從。

translations.literal: Zizhi pressed him, but he never complied.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi pressed him, but he never complied.

sentences.zh: 孝莊為御史中尉，悆兼殿中侍御史，監臨淮王彧軍。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang served as Censor-in-Chief, Yu concurrently served as Palace Attendant Censor, overseeing Prince of Linhuai Yu's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang served as Censor-in-Chief, Yu concurrently served as Palace Attendant Censor, overseeing the army of Prince of Linhuai Yu.

sentences.zh: 時梁遣其豫章王綜據徐州，綜密信通彧，雲欲歸款。

translations.literal: At the time Liang sent its Prince of Yuzhang Zong to hold Xuzhou; Zong secretly sent letters to Yu saying he wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liang sent its Prince of Yuzhang Zong to hold Xuzhou, and Zong secretly sent letters to Yu saying he wished to surrender.

sentences.zh: 眾議謂不然，悆遂請行，曰：「綜若誠心，與之盟約；

translations.literal: The assembly argued it was not so, but Yu then requested to go, saying: "If Zong is sincere, I shall make a pact with him;
translations.idiomatic: The assembly argued otherwise, but Yu then asked to go himself, saying, "If Zong is sincere, I shall make a pact with him;

sentences.zh: 如其詐也，豈惜一人命乎！」

translations.literal: if he is deceitful, what is one man's life to be regretted!"
translations.idiomatic: if he is deceitful, what is one man's life that it should be spared!"

sentences.zh: 時徐州始陷，邊方騷擾，綜部將成景俊、胡龍牙並總強兵，內外嚴固。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhou had just fallen; the frontier was in turmoil; Zong's subordinate generals Cheng Jingjun and Hu Longya both commanded strong troops, and defenses within and without were strict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuzhou had just fallen and the frontier was in turmoil. Zong's subordinate generals Cheng Jingjun and Hu Longya both commanded strong troops, and defenses within and without were strict.

sentences.zh: 悆遂單馬間出，徑趣彭城。

translations.literal: Yu then rode out alone by a hidden route and went straight to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then rode out alone by a hidden route and went straight to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 未至之間，為綜軍主程兵潤所止。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was stopped by Zong's army commander Cheng Bingrun.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he was stopped by Zong's army commander Cheng Bingrun.

sentences.zh: 問其來狀。

translations.literal: He questioned him about the purpose of his coming.
translations.idiomatic: Bingrun questioned him about the purpose of his visit.

sentences.zh: 悆曰：「我為臨淮王所使。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "I am sent by Prince of Linhuai."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "I am sent by Prince of Linhuai."

sentences.zh: 兵潤遣人白龍牙等。

translations.literal: Bingrun sent men to report to Longya and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Bingrun sent men to report to Longya and the others.

sentences.zh: 綜既有誠心，聞悆被執，語景俊等曰：「我每疑元略規欲叛城，將驗虛實，且遣左右為元略使，入魏軍中喚彼一人。

translations.literal: Since Zong already had sincere intent, when he heard Yu had been seized he said to Jingjun and the others: "I have often suspected Yuan Lue was plotting to betray the city; I wish to test whether this is true, and will send attendants posing as Yuan Lue's envoys into the Wei army to summon that one man.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zong already had sincere intent, when he heard Yu had been seized he said to Jingjun and the others, "I have often suspected Yuan Lue was plotting to betray the city. I wish to test whether this is true, and will send attendants posing as Yuan Lue's envoys into the Wei army to summon that one man.

sentences.zh: 其使果至，可令人詐作略身，在一深室，托為患狀，呼使戶外，令人傳語。」

translations.literal: If the envoy truly arrives, one can have someone feign to be Lue himself, in a deep inner room, pretending illness, call the envoy from outside the door, and have another relay the words."
translations.idiomatic: If the envoy truly arrives, someone can feign to be Lue himself in a deep inner room, pretend illness, call the envoy from outside the door, and have another relay the words."

sentences.zh: 時略始被梁武追還。

translations.literal: At that time Lue had just been recalled by Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lue had just been recalled by Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 綜又遣腹心人梁話迎悆，密語意狀，令善酬答。

translations.literal: Zong also sent his trusted man Liang Hua to welcome Yu, secretly explaining the situation and instructing him to answer well.
translations.idiomatic: Zong also sent his trusted man Liang Hua to welcome Yu, secretly explaining the situation and instructing him to answer skillfully.

sentences.zh: 引悆詣龍牙所。

translations.literal: He led Yu to Longya's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He led Yu to Longya's quarters.

sentences.zh: 龍牙語悆曰：「元中山甚欲相見，故令喚卿。」

translations.literal: Longya said to Yu: "Prince of Zhongshan greatly wishes to see you, and so sent for you."
translations.idiomatic: Longya said to Yu, "Prince of Zhongshan greatly wishes to see you, and so sent for you."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「安豐、臨淮，將少弱卒，規復此城，容可得乎？」

translations.literal: He also said: "Anfeng and Linhuai, leading few weak troops, plan to recover this city—can it possibly succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Anfeng and Linhuai, leading a small force of weak troops, plan to recover this city—can that possibly succeed?"

sentences.zh: 悆曰：「彭城，魏之東鄙，勢在必爭，可否在天，非人所測。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Pengcheng is Wei's eastern border; the situation makes it certain to be contested—whether it can be taken lies with Heaven, not something men can measure."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Pengcheng is Wei's eastern border; the situation makes it certain to be contested. Whether it can be taken lies with Heaven, not something men can measure."

sentences.zh: 龍牙曰：「當如卿言。」

translations.literal: Longya said: "It should be as you say."
translations.idiomatic: Longya said, "It should be as you say."

sentences.zh: 復詣景俊住所，停悆外門，久而未入。

translations.literal: He then went to Jingjun's residence, kept Yu at the outer gate, and long went without admitting him.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Jingjun's residence, kept Yu waiting at the outer gate, and long went without admitting him.

sentences.zh: 時夜已久，有綜軍主薑桃來與悆言，謂曰：「元法僧魏之微子，拔城歸梁，梁主待物有道。」

translations.literal: The night was already deep when Zong's army commander Jiang Tao came to speak with Yu, saying: "Yuan Faseng was Wei's Weizi; he abandoned his city and came over to Liang, and the Liang ruler treats men with propriety."
translations.idiomatic: The night was already deep when Zong's army commander Jiang Tao came to speak with Yu, saying, "Yuan Faseng was Wei's Weizi; he abandoned his city and came over to Liang, and the Liang ruler treats men with propriety."

sentences.zh: 乃上指曰：「今歲星在鬥，吳之分野，君何不歸梁國？」

translations.literal: He then pointed upward and said: "This year the Year Star is in the Dipper, the allotted region of Wu—why do you not return to the Liang state?"
translations.idiomatic: He then pointed upward and said, "This year the Year Star is in the Dipper, the allotted region of Wu—why do you not return to the Liang state?"

sentences.zh: 悆答曰：「法僧，莒僕之流，而梁納之，無乃有愧于季孫也！

translations.literal: Yu replied: "Faseng is of the sort of Jufu, yet Liang took him in—is that not a disgrace before Jisun!
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "Faseng is of the sort of Jufu, yet Liang took him in—is that not a disgrace before Jisun!

sentences.zh: 今月建鶉首，斗牛受破，歲星木也，逆而克之，吳國敗喪不久。

translations.literal: This month the station is at Quishou; the Ox and Dipper receive destruction; the Year Star is of wood—going against it to overcome it, Wu's defeat and ruin will come soon.
translations.idiomatic: This month the station is at Quishou; the Ox and Dipper receive destruction; the Year Star is of wood—going against it to overcome it, Wu's defeat and ruin will come soon.

sentences.zh: 且衣錦夜遊，有識不許。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to parade in brocade by night is something no man of discernment would approve."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to parade in brocade by night is something no man of discernment would approve."

sentences.zh: 言未盡，乃引入見景俊。

translations.literal: Before he had finished speaking, they led him in to see Jingjun.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished speaking, they led him in to see Jingjun.

sentences.zh: 景俊良久謂曰：「卿不為刺客也？」

translations.literal: After a long while Jingjun said: "You are not an assassin, are you?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Jingjun said, "You are not an assassin, are you?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「今者為使，欲反命本朝，相刺之事，更卜後圖。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Today I come as an envoy and wish to return and report to my own court; as for assassination, that can be considered on another occasion."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Today I come as an envoy and wish to return and report to my own court; as for assassination, that can be considered on another occasion."

sentences.zh: 為設食，悆強飲多食，向敵數人，微自誇矜。

translations.literal: They set out food; Yu forced himself to drink heavily and eat much, facing several enemies, slightly showing off.
translations.idiomatic: They set out food; Yu forced himself to drink heavily and eat much, facing several enemies across the table, and slightly showed off.

sentences.zh: 諸人相謂曰：「壯哉！」

translations.literal: The men said to one another: "How bold!"
translations.idiomatic: The men said to one another, "How bold!"

sentences.zh: 乃引向元略所，一人引入戶，指床令坐。

translations.literal: They then led him toward Yuan Lue's quarters; one man brought him inside the door and pointed to a bed, telling him to sit.
translations.idiomatic: They then led him toward Yuan Lue's quarters; one man brought him inside the door and pointed to a bed, telling him to sit.

sentences.zh: 一人別在室中出，謂悆曰：「中山王有教：'我昔有以向南，且遣相喚，欲問卿事。

translations.literal: Another came out separately from an inner room and said to Yu: "Prince of Zhongshan has an instruction: 'I once had reason to go south and now send to summon you, wishing to ask you about affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Another came out separately from an inner room and said to Yu, "Prince of Zhongshan has an instruction: 'I once had reason to go south and now send to summon you, wishing to ask you about affairs.

sentences.zh: 晚來患動，不獲相見。

translations.literal: This evening my illness flared up and I could not meet you.
translations.idiomatic: This evening my illness flared up and I could not meet you.

sentences.zh: '遂辭而退。

translations.literal: He then took his leave and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his leave and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 須臾天曉，綜軍主范勖、景俊司馬楊暼票等，競問北朝士馬多少，悆陳士馬之盛。

translations.literal: Before long dawn broke; Zong's army commanders Fan Xu, Jingjun's aide-de-camp Yang Wenpiao, and others all competed in asking how many men and horses the Northern Court had; Yu described their strength in full.
translations.idiomatic: Before long dawn broke; Zong's army commanders Fan Xu, Jingjun's aide-de-camp Yang Wenpiao, and others all competed in asking how many men and horses the Northern Court had, and Yu described their strength in full.

sentences.zh: 尋而與梁話盟契訖。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he completed the covenant with Liang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he completed the covenant with Liang Hua.

sentences.zh: 未旬，綜降詔封悆定陶縣子，除員勻散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Within ten days Zong issued an edict enfeoffing Yu as Viscount of Dingtao and appointing him Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Zong issued an edict enfeoffing Yu as Viscount of Dingtao and appointing him Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 永安中，為右將軍、給事黃門侍郎，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he served as Right General and Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, and was advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he served as Right General and Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate and was advanced in rank to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 雖任居通顯，志在謙退，迎送親賓，加於疇昔。

translations.literal: Although his office was eminent and conspicuous, his intent was humility and withdrawal; in receiving and sending off kin and guests he was more attentive than in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Although his office was eminent and conspicuous, his intent remained humble and retiring; in receiving and sending off kin and guests he was more attentive than in former days.

sentences.zh: 而自無屋宅，常假賃居止，布衣糲食，寒暑不變。

translations.literal: Yet he owned no house of his own, always renting lodgings; coarse cloth and plain food, unchanged in cold or heat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he owned no house of his own and always rented lodgings, wearing coarse cloth and eating plain food unchanged through cold or heat.

sentences.zh: 孝莊嘉其清潔，時復賜以錢帛。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang praised his purity and integrity and from time to time bestowed money and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang praised his purity and integrity and from time to time bestowed money and silk upon him.

sentences.zh: 及東徐城人呂文欣殺刺史元大賓，南引梁人，詔悆以使持節、散騎常侍、安東將軍為六州大使，與行台樊子鵠討破之。

translations.literal: When the people of Dongxu city, Lü Wenxin, killed Governor Yuan Dabin and summoned Liang troops from the south, an edict appointed Yu as envoy bearing credentials, Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Great Envoy of Six Provinces; with Mobile Headquarters Fan Zihu he attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wenxin of Dongxu city killed Governor Yuan Dabin and summoned Liang troops from the south, an edict appointed Yu as envoy bearing credentials, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General Who Pacifies the East, making him Great Envoy of Six Provinces; with Mobile Headquarters Fan Zihu he attacked and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 悆又購斬文欣。

translations.literal: Yu also offered a reward for Wenxin's capture and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yu also offered a reward for Wenxin's capture and execution.

sentences.zh: 還，拜金紫光祿大夫，兼尚書右僕射、東南道三徐行台。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Grand Master of the Purple-Gold Light, concurrently Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Headquarters for the Three Xus of the Southeast Route.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Grand Master of the Purple-Gold Light, concurrently Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Headquarters for the Three Xus of the Southeast Route.

sentences.zh: 與都督賀拔勝等拒爾硃仲遠，軍敗還京。

translations.literal: Together with Area Commander Heba Sheng and others he resisted Erzhu Zhongyuan; the army was defeated and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Area Commander Heba Sheng and others he resisted Erzhu Zhongyuan; the army was defeated and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was appointed Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era he was appointed Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時滎陽人鄭榮業反，圍州城。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Rongye of Xingyang rebelled and besieged the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zheng Rongye of Xingyang rebelled and besieged the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 城降，滎業送悆于關西。

translations.literal: The city surrendered; Rongye sent Yu to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The city surrendered, and Rongye sent Yu to Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 張耀，字景世，自雲南陽西鄂人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yao, style-name Jingshi, was originally a man of Xie in Nanyang of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yao, courtesy name Jingshi, was originally from Xie in Nanyang of Yun.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，累遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He served Wei and was repeatedly promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wei and was repeatedly promoted until he became Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 永寧寺塔大興，經營務廣。

translations.literal: The Yongning Temple pagoda was greatly raised; the works were broad in scope.
translations.idiomatic: Construction of the Yongning Temple pagoda was greatly expanded, and the works were broad in scope.

sentences.zh: 靈太后曾幸作所，凡有顧問，耀敷陳指畫，無所遺闕，太后善之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling once visited the construction site; whenever she asked anything, Yao fully explained and directed, omitting nothing, and the Empress Dowager approved.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling once visited the construction site; whenever she asked anything, Yao fully explained and directed without omitting anything, and the Empress Dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 後為別將，以軍功封長平男。

translations.literal: Later he served as a separate commander and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as a separate commander and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.

sentences.zh: 曆岐、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Qi and Eastern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Governor of Qi and Eastern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天平初，遷鄴草創，右僕射高隆之、吏部尚書元世俊奏曰：「南京宮殿，毀撤送都，連筏竟河，首尾大至，自非賢明一人，專委受納，則恐材木耗損，有關經構。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, when the move to Ye was newly begun, Right Vice Minister Gao Longzhi and Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun memorialized: "The palaces of the Southern Capital are being dismantled and sent to the capital; rafts linked end to end fill the river, great from stem to stern—unless one worthy and clear man is solely entrusted with receiving and storing them, I fear timber will be wasted and construction will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, when the move to Ye was newly begun, Right Vice Minister Gao Longzhi and Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun memorialized, "The palaces of the Southern Capital are being dismantled and sent to the capital; rafts linked end to end fill the river, great from stem to stern—unless one worthy and clear man is solely entrusted with receiving and storing them, I fear timber will be wasted and construction will suffer.

sentences.zh: 耀清直素著，有稱一時，臣等輒舉為大將。」

translations.literal: Yao's purity and uprightness have long been renowned and he is praised throughout the age; we venture to recommend him as Great Commander."
translations.idiomatic: Yao's purity and uprightness have long been renowned and he is praised throughout the age; we venture to recommend him as Great Commander."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 耀勤於其事，尋轉營構左都將。

translations.literal: Yao was diligent in the task and soon was transferred to Left Commander of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was diligent in the task and soon was transferred to Left Commander of Construction.

sentences.zh: 興和初，加衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xinghe he was given the additional title of Defender General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xinghe he was given the additional title of Defender General.

sentences.zh: 宮殿成，除東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When the palaces were completed he was appointed Governor of Eastern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the palaces were completed he was appointed Governor of Eastern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒于州，贈司空公，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the Ministry of Works; posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the Ministry of Works with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 劉道斌，武邑灌津人也。

translations.literal: Liu Daobin was a man of Guanjin in Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daobin was from Guanjin in Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 有器幹，腰帶十圍，須髯甚美。

translations.literal: He had ability and capacity; his belt measured ten wei around; his beard and whiskers were very fine.
translations.idiomatic: He had ability and capacity; his belt measured ten wei around, and his beard and whiskers were very fine.

sentences.zh: 初拜校書郎，轉主書，頗為孝文所知。

translations.literal: At first appointed Collator, then transferred to Master of Documents; he was quite known to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: At first appointed Collator, then transferred to Master of Documents, he came to be well known to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 從征南陽，還，加積射將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Nanyang; on return he was given the additional titles of General of Accumulated Archery and Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Nanyang, and on his return he was given the additional titles of General of Accumulated Archery and Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝謂黃門郎邢巒曰：「道斌是行，便異儕流矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Yellow Gate Gentleman Xing Luan: "In this campaign Daobin has already distinguished himself from his peers."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Yellow Gate Gentleman Xing Luan, "In this campaign Daobin has already distinguished himself from his peers."

sentences.zh: 宣武即位，遷謁者僕射。
