translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu acceded he was transferred to Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu acceded he was transferred to Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 後曆恆農太守、岐州刺史，所在有清貞稱。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Administrator of Hengnong and Governor of Qi; wherever he was, he was praised for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as Administrator of Hengnong and Governor of Qi, and wherever he was he was praised for purity and integrity.

sentences.zh: 卒于州，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was given the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 道斌在恆農，修立學館，建孔子廟堂，圖畫形像。

translations.literal: While Daobin was in Hengnong he established a school hall and built a Confucius temple, painting images.
translations.idiomatic: While Daobin was in Hengnong he established a school hall and built a Confucius temple with painted images.

sentences.zh: 去郡後，故吏追思之，復立道斌形于孔像之西而拜謁焉。

translations.literal: After he left the commandery, former subordinates in longing for him again erected Daobin's image west of Confucius's image and came to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: After he left the commandery, former subordinates, longing for him, again erected Daobin's image west of Confucius's image and came to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 董紹，字興遠，新蔡鮦陽人也。

translations.literal: Dong Shao, style-name Xingyuan, was a man of Ziyang in Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shao, courtesy name Xingyuan, was from Ziyang in Xincai.

sentences.zh: 少好學，頗有文義。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and had considerable literary understanding.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and had considerable literary understanding.

sentences.zh: 起家四門博士，累遷兼中書舍人，為宣武所賞。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Four Gates Doctor and was repeatedly promoted to Concurrent Secretariat Drafter; he was appreciated by Emperor Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a Four Gates Doctor and was repeatedly promoted to Concurrent Secretariat Drafter, and was appreciated by Emperor Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 豫州城人白早生以城南叛，詔紹慰勞，為賊鎖禁送江東。

translations.literal: When Baizaosheng of Yuzhou city rebelled with the south of the city, an edict sent Shao to comfort and reassure; he was chained by the rebels and sent to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Baizaosheng of Yuzhou city rebelled with the south of the city, an edict sent Shao to comfort and reassure the people; he was chained by the rebels and sent to Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 梁領軍呂僧珍暫與紹言，便相器重。

translations.literal: Liang's army commander Lü Sengzhen briefly spoke with Shao and at once valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's army commander Lü Sengzhen briefly spoke with Shao and at once valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 梁武聞之，使勞紹云：「忠臣孝子不可無之，今當聽卿還國。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang heard of this he sent to comfort Shao, saying: "Loyal ministers and filial sons must not be lacking; now I shall allow you to return to your state."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang heard of this he sent to comfort Shao, saying, "Loyal ministers and filial sons must not be lacking; now I shall allow you to return to your state."

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「老母在洛，無復方寸，既奉恩貸，實若更生。」

translations.literal: Shao said: "My old mother is in Luoyang; I have no peace of mind; having received this gracious allowance, it is as if I were born again."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "My old mother is in Luoyang and I have no peace of mind; having received this gracious allowance, it is as if I were born again."

sentences.zh: 乃引見之，謂曰：「戰爭多年，人物塗炭，是以不恥先言，欲與魏朝通好，卿宜備申此意。

translations.literal: He then had him brought in for an audience and said: "War has gone on for many years and the people have been scorched and burned; therefore I am not ashamed to speak first, wishing to establish good relations with the Wei court—you should fully explain this intent.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him brought in for an audience and said, "War has gone on for many years and the people have been scorched and burned; therefore I am not ashamed to speak first, wishing to establish good relations with the Wei court—you should fully explain this intent.

sentences.zh: 若欲通好，今以宿豫還彼，彼當以漢中見歸。」

translations.literal: If you wish good relations, I now return Suyu to them; they should return Hanzhong to us."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish good relations, I now return Suyu to them; they should return Hanzhong to us."

sentences.zh: 及紹還，雖陳說和計，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: When Shao returned, although he set forth the plan for peace, the court did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao returned, although he set forth the plan for peace, the court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 後除洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 紹好行小惠，頗得人情。

translations.literal: Shao liked to perform small favors and won considerable goodwill among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shao liked to perform small favors and won considerable goodwill among the people.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤反于長安，紹上書求擊之，云：「臣當出瞎巴三千，生啖蜀子。」

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled at Chang'an, Shao submitted a memorial requesting to attack him, saying, "Your servant will lead out three thousand blind Ba warriors and devour the Shu men alive."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled at Chang'an, Shao submitted a memorial requesting to attack him, saying, "I will lead out three thousand fierce Ba warriors and devour the Shu rebels alive."

sentences.zh: 孝明謂黃門徐紇曰：「此巴真瞎也？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming said to Xu Zhi of the Yellow Gate, "Are these Ba truly blind?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming said to Xu Zhi of the Yellow Gate, "Are these Ba warriors truly blind?"

sentences.zh: 紇答：「此紹之壯辭，雲巴人勁勇，見敵無所畏，非實瞎也。」

translations.literal: Zhi replied, "This is Shao's bold rhetoric—meaning the Ba are fierce and brave and fear no enemy when they see them; they are not actually blind."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "This is Shao's bold rhetoric—he means the Ba are fierce and brave and fear no enemy; they are not actually blind."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，敕紹速行。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and ordered Shao to depart at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily and ordered Shao to depart at once.

sentences.zh: 以拒寶夤功，賞新蔡縣男。

translations.literal: For his merit in resisting Baoyin he was rewarded with the title Baron of Xincai county.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in resisting Baoyin he was ennobled as Baron of Xincai county.

sentences.zh: 爾硃天光為關右大行台，啟為大行台從事，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Erzhu Tianguang served as western-route grand commissioner; he recommended Shao as staff officer of the grand commission, concurrently director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang served as grand commissioner for the western route, he recommended Shao as staff officer on the grand commission with concurrent appointment as director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 天光敗，賀拔嶽復請紹為其開府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated, Heba Yue again requested Shao as advisory adjutant of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang was defeated, Heba Yue again requested Shao as advisory adjutant on his staff.

sentences.zh: 岳後攜紹于高平牧馬，紹悲而賦詩曰：「走馬山之阿，馬渴飲黃河。

translations.literal: Later Yue took Shao to herd horses at Gaoping; Shao, grieving, composed a poem saying, "Galloping horses on the mountain slope, the horses thirsty drink from the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yue took Shao to herd horses at Gaoping; grieving, Shao composed a poem: "Galloping horses on the mountain slope, thirsty horses drink from the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 甯謂胡關下，復聞楚客歌！」

translations.literal: Could one say that below the Hu passes, the song of the Chu traveler is heard again!"
translations.idiomatic: Can it be that below the Hu passes, the song of the Chu traveler is heard again!"

sentences.zh: 岳死，周文帝亦重之。

translations.literal: When Yue died, Emperor Wen of Zhou also valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue died, Emperor Wen of Zhou also valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，除御史中丞，非其好也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Shao was appointed censor—this was not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Shao was appointed censor—a post that did not suit him.

sentences.zh: 鬱鬱不得志，或行戲街衢，或與少年游聚，不自拘持，頗類失性。

translations.literal: Depressed and unfulfilled, he sometimes played in the streets or gathered with young men in revelry, not restraining himself—rather like one who had lost his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Depressed and unfulfilled, he sometimes played in the streets or gathered with young men in revelry, not restraining himself—almost as if he had lost his true self.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，周文與百官推奉文帝，上表勸進，令呂思禮、薛憕作表，前後再奏，帝尚執謙沖不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Zhou Wen and the hundred officials urged Emperor Wen to ascend, submitting memorials to encourage his advance; he ordered Lü Sil and Xue Kui to compose the memorials, and after two submissions the emperor still held to modest refusal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Zhou Wen and the hundred officials urged Emperor Wen to ascend the throne, submitting memorials encouraging his advance; he had Lü Sil and Xue Kui compose the memorials, and after two submissions the emperor still modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「為文能動至尊，唯董公耳！」

translations.literal: Zhou Wen said, "In literary power to move the supreme sovereign, only Duke Dong!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen said, "Only Duke Dong can write words that move the supreme sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 乃命紹為第三表，操筆便成。

translations.literal: He then ordered Shao to compose the third memorial; taking up the brush, it was finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Shao to compose the third memorial; Shao took up the brush and finished it at once.

sentences.zh: 表奏，周文曰：「開進人意，不當如此也？」

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, Zhou Wen said, "To open the mind toward advance—should it not be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was presented, Zhou Wen said, "To open his mind toward accepting the throne—should it not be like this?"

sentences.zh: 及登祚，方任用之，而紹議論朝廷，賜死。

translations.literal: When the throne was taken, he was only then put to use, but Shao criticized the court in discussion and was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Once the throne was taken, he was finally put to use, but Shao criticized the court in discussion and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 孫嗣。

translations.literal: His son Si succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Si succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 時有濟郡曹昂，有學識，舉秀才。

translations.literal: At that time there was Cao Ang of Ji commandery, learned and accomplished, recommended as cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Cao Ang of Ji commandery, a learned man who was recommended as cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 永安中，除太學博士，兼尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was appointed academician of the Imperial University, concurrently director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he was appointed academician of the Imperial University with concurrent appointment as a director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 常徒步上省，以示清貧，忽遇盜，大失綾縑，時人鄙其矯詐。

translations.literal: He often went on foot to the provincial offices to display purity and poverty; suddenly he encountered robbers and lost a great quantity of silk brocade—men of the time despised his pretense and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: He often walked on foot to the provincial offices to display his purity and poverty; suddenly he was robbed and lost a great quantity of silk brocade—men of the time despised his hypocrisy.

sentences.zh: 論曰：孫紹關左之士，又能指論時務。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Sun Shao was a man of the western passes who could also point out and discuss affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment says: Sun Shao was a man of the western passes who could also point out and discuss affairs of the age.

sentences.zh: 張普惠明達典故，強直從官，侃然不撓，其有王臣之風矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Puhui was clear in classical precedents, upright as a attendant official, bold and unyielding—he had the bearing of a true minister of the king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Puhui was clear in classical precedents, upright as a remonstrating official, bold and unyielding—he had the bearing of a true royal minister.

sentences.zh: 成淹、范紹、劉桃符、鹿悆、張耀、劉道斌、董紹、馮元興等，身遭際會，俱得效其所能，苟曰非才，亦何能致於此也。

translations.literal: Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Lu Yu, Zhang Yao, Liu Daobin, Dong Shao, Feng Yuanxing, and the rest—all encountered their moment and were able to display their abilities; if one says they lacked talent, how could they have reached such positions?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Lu Yu, Zhang Yao, Liu Daobin, Dong Shao, Feng Yuanxing, and the rest—all encountered their moment and were able to display their abilities; if one says they lacked talent, how could they have reached such heights?
